items.summary: A scandal involving Nvidia's chief executive could affect the broader technology sector, according to a report. NPR's Sacha Pfeiffer spoke with Bloomberg tech reporter Ian King about Jensen Huang's outsized influence at his company and across American tech.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal May Have Wide - Ranging Implications for Tech Industry

items.summary: Anthropic and its co-founders are seeking to raise as much as $90.4 billion through an IPO and private placement, per a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday. The base offering would reach up to $64.4 billion at share prices of $70 to $78 each, while backers sell 23.6 million shares privately for $26 billion in aggregate. With an over-allotment option, Bloomberg News calculations show the total could hit roughly $100 billion, topping SpaceX's base offering or its greenshoe-raised amount. The IPO is set to price on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and trade the following day.
items.title: Anthropic Plans $90.4 Billion IPO at $1.4 Trillion Valuation

items.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, OpenAI's third-quarter revenue rose about 50 per cent to roughly $10 billion while its operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion. The company reported an adjusted operating margin improving to -109 per cent from -150 per cent in the prior quarter, though it did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
items.title: OpenAI Posts Steep Losses as Revenue Climbs Toward $10 Billion

items.summary: IBM announced Tuesday it is ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people. The change follows scrutiny from Donald Trump's administration over foreign tech hiring, including last month's suspension of Microsoft, Adobe and several outsourcers from the Permanent Labor Certification process.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa Sponsorship For Most Consulting Roles

items.summary: Amazon announced two new Ring security products, an AI-powered drone camera expected in early 2027 and a robot cam starting end of 2026. The devices use on-device sensors and cloud processing to map spaces and plan patrols autonomously. Amazon noted the drone still needs FCC authorization before its January 27, 2027 sale target. The announcement raised new privacy concerns beyond existing fixed-camera worries.
items.title: Amazon Unveils AI Security Drone and Robot for Ring Customers

items.summary: Joon Kim, a former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York who previously led investigations that ended in convictions and resignations, has been tapped to lead an internal probe into Nvidia’s chief executive Jensen Huang. The assignment follows Huang’s Sunday admission of an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, raising questions about whether he compromised trade secrets or national security interests amid reports of foreign influence campaigns. Nvidia says it has no reason to believe either was breached; shares fell 10% since the disclosure, removing $500 billion from its market value.
items.title: Nvidia Names Former Prosecutor Joon Kim To Probe CEO Jensen Huang

items.summary: OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to its founder Francis Davidson, who now works for the lab. The deal terms were not disclosed and look like an acqui-hire; OpenAI confirmed the hire but announced no new travel-specific products or plans. Davidson previously founded Sonder in 2014, which reached $143 million in revenues before bankruptcy. Odessia raised a $6 million pre-seed round led by Sequoia about five months ago and had helped plan millions of dollars' worth of travel before shutting down.
items.title: OpenAI Acquires AI Travel Startup Odessia in Acquihire

items.summary: Anthropic introduced upgraded Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models, reporting that over 1000 AI agents built an operating system prototype in eight days under its guidance. The company says the software started about 26 times faster and the models also improved cybersecurity research, though it still recommends older tools for everyday coding.
items.title: Anthropic's Claude models claim operating-system build by AI agents

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, is at the center of a scandal involving an alleged affair with Alice Huang, who leads Megaspeed and faces suspected ties to Chinese intelligence. Experts worry his advocacy for loosening advanced chip export restrictions may have been influenced by the relationship. The Trump administration reportedly knew about the connection but did not warn him; despite FBI involvement and assurances from both Trump and Nvidia's board that no secrets were compromised, officials say these claims fail to ease concerns.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Espionage Scandal Allegations Over China Ties

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Apple will charge a one-time $50 fee, rather than a subscription, to grant server-based AI capacity in Creator Studio apps. The fee applies to extra usage blocks when users exceed set limits and is intended to help offset the cost of running large language models. Logic Pro packs are available now; other apps follow soon. Packs expire after 12 months but roll over monthly if unused.
items.title: Apple Introduces One-Time $50 Fee for AI Usage Packs

items.summary: US stocks dropped on Nov 10 after the Labour Department reported that the Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% in October, its third straight gain of at least that size and above the 0.3% estimate polled by Reuters economists, following a 0.6% rise in September. Fed governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise borrowing costs in December even if inflation cooled, or consider an upsized half-point hike if it worsens. Markets now price at least a 25 basis point increase, up from 84% on Nov 9 per CME FedWatch. The Dow fell 223.12 points, or 0.43%, to 52,166.63; the S&P 500 lost 48.06 points, or 0.64%, to 7,501.88; and the Nasdaq Composite fell 290.69 points, or 1.15%, to 24,962.44.
items.title: US stocks fell as hot inflation data raised Fed rate-hike odds

items.summary: Nvidia's shares fell about 5.5% on Monday, cutting its market value by roughly $260 billion as CEO Jensen Huang became embroiled in an alleged spying controversy in Taiwan. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation; reports say no evidence supports claims of a national-security breach.
items.title: Nvidia faces $26 billion market drop amid espionage probe over Jensen Huang

items.summary: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) registered a suo motu case after receiving three alerts about suspected online circulation of child sexual abuse material. The alerts came from the US-based National Centre for Missing and Exploited Children through the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre, which routed them to Indian authorities. After preliminary checks of IP addresses, mobile numbers and email IDs, officials filed an FIR under Section 67B of the Information Technology Act.
items.title: Telangana Cyber Bureau Closes Google Alerts Case

items.summary: Nvidia retained law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz on Tuesday to lead an independent investigation its board announced Sunday into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence considers a Chinese spy. The Wall Street Journal reports Joon Kim will head the inquiry; Nvidia stock fell about 6% that day. In a note to employees, Huang wrote his actions hurt her and their children. Rosen Law Firm filed a shareholder class action against both men in San Jose federal court.
items.title: Nvidia Retains Wachtell Lipton to Lead Jensen Huang Affair Probe

items.summary: Following quarterly results that lifted Titan shares 3.6% over three sessions, the company points to studded jewellery as a key growth driver, which now accounts for 35% of sales after growing 32% year-on-year versus 16% a year earlier. Premium watches and eyewear are also expected to help, while Motilal Oswal Financial Services maintains a Buy rating at Rs 5,700 and Prabhudas Lilladher downgraded the stock to Accumulate with a target of Rs 5,330.
items.title: Titan Eyes Studded Jewellery, Watches and Eyewear for Growth

items.summary: Adoring fans follow Jensen Huang on his visits, a trend domestic media call 'Jensanity'. Shock is palpable in Taipei businesses after news that both Nvidia's board and the FBI are investigating whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence. Taiwan's government has declined to address details directly; Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi said he had no evidence or authority to investigate. Academic Liu I-li, 49, urged broader judgment of people beyond one flaw.
items.title: Taiwan Fans React as Nvidia CEO Faces Spy Probe

items.summary: The US House of Representatives voted 211-204, with more than a dozen members including 11 Democrats absent, to refer impeachment articles against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Republican-led House Judiciary Committee - effectively killing the effort introduced by Congressman Thomas Massie. Hegseth dismissed it as sabotage; President Trump mocked Massie and celebrated the defeat.
items.title: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, for now

items.summary: The National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) warned that the Bank of England's hesitant response to rising inflation risks higher interest rates for longer. After raising borrowing costs from 3.75% to 4%, Niesr director David Aikman said a timid increase may keep inflation above the 2% target until at least 2030, with UK inflation currently standing at 3.5%. The institute expects growth of 1.6% this year but only 0.9% in 2028 as high inflation and rates weigh on confidence.
items.title: Thinktank Warns Bank of England Risks Prolonged High Interest Rates

items.summary: A report by the parliamentary and health service ombudsman for England, Paula Sussex, says disabled people in England can wait up to two years for a wheelchair because of delays involving NHS bodies and private firms. In one case Elliot Cruz Gardiyanoglu waited seven months before nursery started; his mother Jania Cruz said they were never told the delay would be so long. Graham Woolner received a faulty device 26 months past an 18-week deadline. Sussex points to a regulatory gap in assessment, fitting and repair.
items.title: England's Disabled People Face Wheelchair Delays of Up to Two Years, Ombudsman Report Finds

items.summary: Israeli ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot and allies launched a legislative onslaught against caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s legacy when the new Knesset convened in a heated first session. His Yashar party submitted proposals, including an independent commission to investigate security failures that allowed the Hamas attack of Oct. 7, 2023 — which Netanyahu has long opposed.
items.title: Eisenkot bloc opens new Israeli parliament with attacks on Netanyahu

items.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday it completed distributions from a $40 million Fair Fund created after Elon Musk settled the regulator's first civil enforcement case against him for securities fraud over an August 7, 2018 post that he had
items.title: SEC Closes $40 Million Musk Settlement Fund

items.summary: Security firm Claroc reports that Grok Build, a coding agent from SpaceXSI (the merged SpaceX and xAI), leaks user data through shareable app links. The exposure includes internal business plans, ad proposals, medical results, employee names and IDs—some from 24 SpaceXSI apps. After notifying the company with no response, Claroc tagged Musk and Grok Manager Matt Palmer on X. Most data remained accessible until SpaceXSI removed links within hours of Ars contacting them.
items.title: SpaceXSI Grok Build App Data Leak

items.summary: IBM announced Tuesday it is discontinuing visa and green card sponsorship across its largest division, a move the company framed as supporting the Trump administration's efforts to limit corporate hiring of foreign workers. The White House has proposed $100,000 filing fees for H-1B visas, which critics call a tax on foreign talent. Separately, President Donald Trump acknowledged his immigration enforcement had been “too tough” before walking back the remark.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa Sponsorship in Largest Division Amid Trump Immigration Push

items.summary: In its S-1 filing, Anthropic disclosed that each of its seven co-founders plans to sell 3,378,378 shares. At the midrange price of $74, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million; at $70, over $236 million, and at $78, under $264 million. Board members Reed Hastings and Christopher Liddell also plan to buy shares worth $300 million and $3 million respectively.
items.title: Anthropic Founders Set for $250M IPO Windfalls

items.summary: Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, bundling this month's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes with additional bug fixes. The update targets users on Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC or enrolled in the ESU program and moves affected systems to builds 19045.7846 and 19044.7846 respectively. It addresses 1,235 vulnerabilities across Microsoft's products, including one actively exploited Outlook zero-day flaw, plus fixes for printing, Remote Desktop, PowerShell script signing, and USB audio issues previously introduced by September updates.
items.title: Microsoft Ships Windows 10 Security Update With Patch Tuesday Fixes

items.summary: A threat actor exploited compromised Qubole IAM credentials to access and exfiltrate data across multiple customers' AWS environments between October 14 and 26. The attack leveraged cross-account trust roles, with Sentra reporting dozens of victims and millions of files stolen from one customer alone. Researchers at Wiz and Mandiant documented the method; exact compromise details remain unspecified.
items.title: Qubole AWS Trust Misconfiguration Enables Multi-Tenant Data Breach

items.summary: Microsoft researchers describe “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that reprograms dormant neurons in an LLM so an otherwise normal agent executes malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The attack requires no training, can be inserted without retraining the model, and passes standard safety evaluations while quietly downloading attacker code or running destructive commands with whatever access it has. Researchers say fewer than 10 reprogrammed dormant neurons suffice to backdoor an agent built on them. They note that frontier agents may detect anomalous weight edits if asked, but no scan can prove a model is safe beyond doubt; provenance and weight integrity matter. Microsoft Foundry verifies model provenance, ties models to trusted publishers, scans the software environment before onboarding open-weight models, and is developing AI-powered weight scanning, red-teaming tools, and cryptographic signing with tamper-evident audit trails.
items.title: Microsoft Researchers Detail Lazarus AI Backdoor Technique

items.summary: Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer accused President Donald Trump on Tuesday of dereliction of duty after reports that Trump was told over a year earlier about an alleged affair involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and someone suspected of spying for China, yet took no action. The remarks were made by Schumer, a New York Democrat, on the Senate floor.
items.title: Schumer Calls Trump's Nvidia Affair Inaction a Dereliction of Duty

items.summary: A ForeCast episode of Forethought's interview podcast features Avi Parrack, a former researcher at the think tank, and Tom Davidson, a senior research fellow there. They discuss whether SpaceX could reach around 99% of global launch capacity once Starship flies, how Golden Dome interceptors would work, rival countermeasures like jamming and lasers, and whether such dominance might shape US–China relations.
items.title: Forethought podcast on US space and launch dominance

items.summary: Unity Catalog metric views, part of Databricks' open and governed semantic layer built on the lakehouse, are now available in Power BI through a feature called Publish to Power BI. The capability lets organizations define business KPIs once in Databricks while using Power BI as their front end for reports, notebooks, AI dashboards, and Genie agents. Each metric view becomes one table in the semantic model, with its dimensions becoming columns and measures translated into DAX automatically; joins run in Databricks so definitions stay consistent everywhere consumers read them. Publish to Power BI is currently available in Private Preview.
items.title: Databricks Brings Unity Catalog Metric Views to Power BI

items.summary: In a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Anthropic said it plans to raise up to $64 billion through its initial public offering, valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion. The debut price estimate sits between $70.00 and $78.00 per share. Earlier estimates had placed the valuation as high as $2 trillion before slipping amid falling AI stock prices.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for $1.4 Trillion Valuation in IPO

items.summary: AI agents spend much of their time idle, and Kubernetes was not built to serve that pattern. NVIDIA's open-source runtime Agent Substrate now donated to the CNCF Sandbox runs sandboxed agents with 10x higher density than standard containers by multiplexing many sessions over a small pool of worker Pods and checkpointing idle state including memory and filesystem. It is security-hardened, zero-trust software engineered for millions of agents and tools. NVIDIA contributes upstream as agentic infrastructure moves toward proprietary runtimes that bypass Kubernetes. The project targets coding assistants, reinforcement learning post-training with CPU-heavy environments alongside GPU trainers, and research GPU sandboxes.
items.title: NVIDIA Donates Agent Substrate Runtime for Scaling AI Agents on Kubernetes

items.summary: Delhi's air quality worsened after Diwali as firecracker emissions accounted for more than 80% of the city's pollution load on Monday, per models from the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology. Cleaner conditions followed due to favourable winds that dispersed accumulated pollutants and limited stubble smoke intrusion from neighbouring states.
items.title: Fireworks drove Delhi pollution on Monday

items.summary: A forum contributor argues that walking ability is a better health indicator than grip strength, despite the latter's association with mortality. Citing a 2015 Lancet study of 139,691 people, they note local Singaporean Timed Up and Go times average 9.8 seconds versus a commonly cited Western figure of 12.3, warning that foreign thresholds may miss at-risk individuals. The piece also highlights walking-while-talking as an accessible memory test, suggesting observation during everyday walks over dynamometer measurements.
items.title: Walking ability may outperform grip strength as a health marker

items.summary: The VHP accused Sonia Gandhi on Tuesday of selective outrage, demanding an apology for statements it said hurt Hindus. Surendra Jain questioned why she mourned the Babri demolition but not more than 350 temples demolished in Kashmir or massacres in Bastar and Delhi in 1984. The party framed her reaction as inconsistent across these events.
items.title: VHP Accuses Sonia Gandhi of Selective Outrage Over Hindu Sites and Massacres

items.summary: Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang admitted in an employee message on November 8, 2026, that he had been unfaithful to his wife. The admission followed reports of a possible Chinese spy plot involving Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, whom US intelligence officials reportedly assessed as funneling information to Beijing. Nvidia's board launched an independent investigation and stated it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised; the inquiry is being overseen by outside counsel with Huang cooperating. The matter drew attention from President Donald Trump, who said he believes Huang did not know of her alleged links and that FBI involvement suggests Huang will be in good shape.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Admits Affair and Faces Foreign-Spy Probe

items.summary: A TOI correspondent in Washington reports that President Donald Trump repeatedly vouched for Nvidia chief Jensen Huang after disclosures he may have been caught in a Chinese honey-trap. Speaking at the White House on Monday, Trump called Huang “a great, brilliant person” and recounted asking him whether he knew his affair partner was allegedly a spy; Huang reportedly replied, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’ The remarks come as lawmakers investigate Trump-linked accounts that filings show bought between $500,001 and $1 million of Nvidia shares on January 6, 2026, and more later. Senator Chris Coons wants an inquiry into ties to foreign intelligence operatives. Tech analysts meanwhile scrutinize Huang’s advocacy for selling advanced chips to China. Trump said he believes Huang is ‘very above board,’ though the White House says third parties manage the portfolio without presidential input.
items.title: Trump Defends Nvidia Chief Amid China Spy Probe and Trading Scrutiny

items.summary: In Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi reflects on becoming one of India's most consequential political figures against deep private grief. The 502-page memoir opens with the morning of 31 October 1984, when she heard shots as her mother-in-law Indira Gandhi was assassinated by two Sikh bodyguards in retaliation for the army's storming of the Golden Temple. She pleaded that leaders wanted her husband Rajiv to become prime minister; he replied: 'They will kill me anyway.' That evening he was sworn in. Rajiv died in 1991, and Sonia later declined office after Congress's 2004 election victory, choosing Manmohan Singh instead. The book also offers a direct portrait of Narendra Modi and notes the memoir sidesteps Congress's own record of corruption.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi's memoir recounts her rise amid personal loss

items.summary: The Strait of Hormuz stays one of the most dangerous sea routes, with ships still attacked despite US Navy help and mines possibly lurking beneath. Steve Cameron says captains weigh war risk insurance before transiting. Ian McFarlane of Thales notes mines are a cheap naval tool. Traditionally specialist vessels crewed by about 80 sailors hunted them; now autonomous systems monitored from shore may need only around 20 land-based personnel, appealing amid recruitment strains in Nato navies. The latest Gulf conflict tests capable craft like Anduril's XLUUV and Thales's USV. Steve Prest of RUSI says robots reduce risk but are applications on a wider cognitive architecture. Insurers at Lloyd's say the Omani route runs at about 75% of pre-conflict levels, with fear of unknown mines driving demand for robotic solutions.
items.title: Robot vessels take on mine hunting in the Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: Toy sales in the UK are rising ahead of the Christmas period, according to research company Circana. Figures show that toys sold up to October were 17% higher than the same period last year, with growth at a 10-year high despite cost-of-living pressures. The kidult market has also grown, and traditional play remains popular as connected toys account for less than 1% of sales.
items.title: Traditional Toys Drive UK Sales Ahead of Christmas

items.summary: Analysts say a cyberattack on supermarket refrigerators that France blames on Iran marks a new phase in Tehran's asymmetric campaign against the United States, extending it onto European soil. Scores of French supermarkets were hit in October 2025 attacks that raised refrigerator temperatures and forced some to discard perishable inventories. France says Iran's Revolutionary Guard was behind what officials call unprecedented cyberattacks; Iran rejected the charge.
items.title: France Blames Iran for Supermarket Refrigerator Hack Marking New Phase in Asymmetric Campaign

items.summary: Border communities across Texas voted overwhelmingly for Democratic candidates, giving the party control of all 18 statewide races and both chambers of Congress. Despite these wins, advocates say the Trump administration retains funding—$46.5 billion from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act—and legal authority to continue building border barriers in ecologically sensitive areas like Big Bend. Land Commissioner-elect Ben Flores pledged not to grant access on his office's land, while state legislators introduced bills to bar construction in parks. The Supreme Court overturned a temporary injunction Monday, allowing work to resume.
items.title: Texas Democrats Seek Ways to Block Border Wall in Big Bend

items.summary: Peter Lewis argues Anthony Albanese's relationship with Australia's music industry is strained by the government's approach to artificial intelligence, which he frames as a threat to creativity. The column contends that Anthropic, an AI company seeking roughly $1.5tn valuation, has proposed training models in Australia while relaxing copyright protections, prompting creators to warn this would make the country a haven for data-washing. Lewis cites concerns from Nick Cave about replication and broader worries across mathematics, education and psychology. He frames the issue as more than intellectual property, arguing creatives deserve control over their work and meaningful reparation, and calls for clear labelling of human content rather than accepting AI's terms.
items.title: Albanese faces creative sector backlash over AI copyright plans

items.summary: A Mint analysis of annual reports from 232 BSE 500 companies found that nearly 45% of executive heads earned more than 100 times the company's median employee remuneration in FY26, up from nearly 40% in FY20. Experts attribute rising pay to stronger corporate growth, greater business complexity and a tight supply of qualified leaders. Director compensation rose 38% year-on-year against a 22% rise in aggregate net profit, while regular employee wages grew just 1%. The gap raises questions about wealth distribution and fairness, with some warning it may dampen morale as scrutiny from investors intensifies.
items.title: India's Top Executives Pull Further Ahead of Workers on Pay

items.summary: Tech companies want agentic AI to become the new way people shop, but NPR raises whether that should be trusted when money is involved. The piece frames this as a direct question rather than offering conclusions or evidence about reliability.
items.title: Should you trust new AI agents with your money and data?

items.summary: Canadian wildlife services euthanized four grizzly bears, including three cubs, following the deaths of a mother and daughter mauled to death in western Canada. DNA tests confirmed the animals were responsible for the attack. Authorities warn that grizzly bears can be aggressive during this time of year.
items.title: Four bears euthanized after fatal mauling in Canada

items.summary: An unusual decline in humpbacks during their annual migration along Western Australia's coast has concerned marine scientists, who say the trend reflects a broader drop in Southern Hemisphere sightings and rising strandings. A Broome tour operator reports fewer whales, forcing tours to travel much further afield.
items.title: Marine scientists alarmed by declining humpback whale numbers off Western Australia

items.summary: The BBC Radio 4 programme Tech Life, presented by Chris Vallance with Imran Rahman-Jones as producer, investigates how everyday connected devices are vulnerable to a wave of cyber-attacks targeting commercial refrigerators in Europe. The episode also includes listener contributions about moderating an adult service and the impact of US Midterm elections on global technology.
items.title: Tech Life explores cyber-attacks on smart fridges and more

items.summary: The Election Commission of India told the Delhi High Court it is awaiting a verification report before deciding whether to register Waris Punjab De as a political party. The commission received sensitive information about alleged separatist links and past affiliations, including claims that founders were detained under the National Security Act. It forwarded objections to Punjab’s Chief Electoral Officer on July 14, 2026, who was directed to conduct an inquiry; reminders have been sent but no report has arrived.
items.title: Election Commission Awaits Report on Waris Punjab De Separatist Allegations

items.summary: Annette Young introduces James Townsend, Atlantic Council senior advisor at the Scowcroft Center's Transatlantic Security Initiative. Townsend says Europe is not going anywhere and that a Paris meeting signals to Russia that Western support remains durable. He argues the gathering tests Western cohesion and future military aid rather than being only diplomacy.
items.title: Atlantic Council's Townsend frames G7 summit as signal of European resolve for Ukraine

items.summary: Amid growing strains on global trade and investment, Bert Hofman argues that Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) holds real value not through signing agreements but by providing a forum where major competitors can still work together. Speaking as former World Bank country director for China, Mongolia and Korea, he says the most important outcome of this year's APEC meeting in Shenzhen is trust: trust in trade, and trust in the power of international cooperation.
items.title: Bert Hofman on APEC's Role in Global Trade Cooperation

items.summary: French police raided three properties, including Paris's Ritz hotel and two Saint-Tropez villas linked to Mohamed Al Fayed, during a preliminary investigation into alleged human trafficking, aggravated pimping and rape. Searches occurred on 13 and 14 October amid British Metropolitan Police involvement. Survivors' groups urge the National Crime Agency to take over; the Met is investigating 169 direct contacts while more than 500 women have reportedly come forward.
items.title: French Police Raid Fayed-Linked Properties in Abuse Probe

items.summary: Chief Minister Hemant Soren ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the death of 39-year-old tribal activist Nisha Bhagat, who died allegedly by suicide on November 6 after accusing the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha-led government and land brokers of harassment. The National Commission for Scheduled Tribe directed officials to submit a report within seven days or face legal action, while police registered an FIR against two people.
items.title: Jharkhand CM Orders CBI Probe Into Tribal Activist Death

items.summary: The Spanish royal couple joined relatives of the dead at a solemn funeral Mass in Toledo's 13th-century cathedral, nearly two weeks after one of Europe's deadliest rail disasters this century. Residents of Urda placed 69 candles near the altar and brought a 16th-century sculpture of Christ for the ceremony. Spain's second fatal high-speed rail accident this year has left 69 people dead after a Renfe train collided with a stationary Iryo service near Urda on 28 October, prompting resignations and an EU safety funds probe; Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez did not attend citing his refusal to join religious ceremonies as the election approaches.
items.title: Spanish royals attend funeral Mass for train crash victims in Toledo cathedral

items.summary: A study published in Molecular Ecology proposes that the chytrid fungus Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis caused historic amphibian declines in Brazil’s Atlantic Forest during the 1970s and ’80s. Researchers analyzed specimens collected before and after the decline, finding no trace of Bd in 1978 but widespread presence from 1983 onward. First author Jack Boyette noted the appearance coincides with the declines. However, some scientists dispute this link; Lucas Ferrante argues detecting a pathogen does not prove it caused the decline. The study also highlights species resilience at Boracéia research station and offers methods for historical disease research.
items.title: New Research Links Fungus To Historic Amphibian Declines In Brazil

items.summary: Sophos Counter Threat Unit Director Rafe Pilling discusses how states increasingly use cyberattacks to support broader objectives. He cites supermarket refrigeration system attacks in France as an example, noting that adversaries can create large impacts with minimal effort by destroying food and leaving store shelves empty.
items.title: Sophos Expert Explains Rise of Asymmetric Cyberwarfare

items.summary: Wells Fargo upgraded US AI infrastructure stocks to neutral after semiconductor shares fell about 38% from June highs, with valuation multiples contracting. Analysts said current prices already reflect expected slowdowns in AI-related earnings growth and that risk-reward is reasonable. The sell-off erased about $3 trillion from S&P 500 companies, partly driven by midterm-election concerns over tighter data-centre regulation.
items.title: Wells Fargo Trims AI Infrastructure Stock Ratings After Chip Drop

items.summary: OpenAI's third-quarter revenue reached US$10 billion (S$12.8 billion), a nearly 50% rise from the prior quarter, driven by strong demand for its latest AI software, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity because the figures are not public. The details were shared with investors during a Nov. 10 call; OpenAI declined to comment.
items.title: OpenAI Q3 Revenue Surges Nearly 50% Past $10 Billion

items.summary: Meta introduces Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX), a hardware-native compiler extension that adds explicit warp-group and cluster-level orchestration to the Triton programming model, letting ML engineers adopt modern NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell features without leaving Python. The authors report using it in production across Meta’s recommendation systems and large-scale LLM pretraining. In GEM training they cite O(10^24) total training flops with 20-25% end-to-end MFU, near-optimal performance on a generalized dot-product attention kernel (up to 2x forward speedup), a 4x speedup from an in-kernel broadcast optimization on the H100, and up to two-thirds reduction in net latency for co-designed FlashAttention kernels. TLX is positioned as occupying the middle ground between CUDA’s control and Triton’s productivity.
items.title: Meta Ships TLX Compiler for Production GPU Workloads

items.summary: According to documents viewed by The Wall Street Journal, OpenAI reported an adjusted operating margin improving to -109% from -150%, while its operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion in the prior quarter. Reuters sought comment; OpenAI did not respond immediately. The disclosure arrives as investors scrutinize AI finances, including Anthropic's potential IPO valued at about $1.4 trillion.
items.title: OpenAI posts steep losses even as quarterly revenue rises to $10 billion

items.summary: Unplugged Performance publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors. The pitch came four days after Elon Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with sales running at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for. UP says it supports prioritizing Cybercab and would run the truck “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus,” while collecting a license fee plus FSD and Robotaxi revenue. The post passed 240,000 views within hours; neither Musk nor Tesla had responded at writing. Electrek notes demand is the real problem: Q3 saw 8,295 Other Models delivered, about 7,000 to 8,000 of which were Cybertrucks — a pace of roughly 30,000 trucks a year — even though Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet and the line runs at about a quarter of its 125,000-unit capacity.
items.title: Tesla Tuner Offers to Take Over Cybertruck Production

items.summary: According to a Bloomberg report, Anthropic PBC is seeking about $1.4 trillion valuation in an initial public offering that could make it the first frontier AI laboratory to go public. The company and some backers aim to raise as much as $90.4 billion through the IPO and private placement.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Record IPO

items.summary: Nvidia said on Tuesday it hired New York-based Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead a thorough and independent investigation into allegations surrounding chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, accused of spying for China. Nvidia's shares fell close to a one-year low, wiping about $500 billion (£375 billion) off its market value since Friday.
items.title: Nvidia Hires Law Firm Over CEO Spy Allegations

items.summary: A survey commissioned by Syfe and conducted by YouGov among Singaporean adults found that major life expenses, such as buying a first home or raising children, slow investing momentum even though many want to invest more. About 65% of those who saw their first job as their biggest financial milestone invested more later, versus 49% in Hong Kong and 42% in Australia. Confidence falls sharply with age: 40% of Singaporeans aged 18 to 24 are highly confident about investing, but only 12% among those above 55. The survey suggests the challenge is helping people feel informed enough to stay invested through life's stages.
items.title: Singaporeans Want More Investing But Life Costs Hold Them Back

items.summary: IBM said it discontinued visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division of over 150,000 workers. Impacted employees may keep working outside the US or leave by year's end. The move follows pressure from the Trump administration on tech firms to hire American staff amid immigration concerns.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa Sponsorship in Largest Unit

items.summary: A California judge found Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation in a lawsuit brought by Ambrose Conroy of Rancho Santa Fe, whose never-completed Solar Roof failed to generate electricity. The ruling follows repeated failures by the company to produce documents during discovery, including internal messages describing the project as an experiment. Judge Cynthia Freeland rejected Tesla's request to reconsider the decision on October 27.
items.title: California judge finds Tesla liable for Solar Roof fraud

items.summary: Official data shows China's trade surplus exceeded $US1 trillion in the first 10 months, surpassing last year's record. Exports rose 35.2 per cent to $US412.3 billion and imports grew 41.6 per cent to $US307.1 billion. The boom is driven by AI-related products amid weak domestic demand, as Beijing relies on exports toward its 4.5-5.0 per cent growth target while trade tensions with the US and EU persist.
items.title: China's Trade Surplus Tops $1 Trillion for Second Straight Year

items.summary: Yasodara Cordova argues Brazil's AI strategy overemphasizes frontier models and data centers, ignoring edge computing. The country announced 2.3 billion reais ($444.2 million) for supercomputing projects [quantity-641-658][quantity-660-674]. A July 2026 Getulio Vargas Foundation study estimated that only about 4% of a model's jobs become permanent roles, versus 85% tied to construction [date-5581-5585][entity-5586-5617][quantity-5678-5681][quantity-5745-5747]. Meanwhile, the federal Nova Indústria Brasil policy set aside 300 billion reais through 2026 [date-6324-6328][entity-6245-6272][quantity-6347-6364]. Cordova contends edge AI better suits Brazil's industrial needs and existing repair workforce, though the government currently favors centralized infrastructure.
items.title: Brazil's AI Plan Should Embrace Edge Computing Over Data Centers

items.summary: Nima Momeni was sentenced to 16 years to life in the murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee, convicted by a jury of second-degree murder. The killing occurred on 4 April 2023 under the Bay Bridge after an alleged feud surfaced during the trial. During sentencing, Lee’s daughter Scout Lee and Momeni’s mother Mahnaz Tayarani spoke to the judge, while Momeni expressed remorse.
items.title: Man Sentenced for Killing Cash App Founder Bob Lee

items.summary: Macquarie Bank will pay a court-imposed civil penalty after admitting it broke the Corporations Act through its welcome rate promotions. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission pursued action over savings conditions that risked short-changing customers amid rising living costs. Macquarie said in court proceedings it failed to provide financial services efficiently, honestly and fairly.
items.title: Macquarie Bank Faces $14m Penalty Over Confusing Savings Promotion

items.summary: The US Department of Justice announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives alleged to have taken part in a series of plots across the US and Europe. The indictment accuses them, most recently, of orchestrating an attack at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire in September 2026, where seven men were arrested. Iranian officials deny involvement. Kash Patel said the accused supported Iran's IRGC and Kataib Hezbollah in nearly 20 attempted attacks, while a DOJ statement noted that HAYI claimed responsibility for 18 of those attacks across Europe, seven in the UK.
items.title: US Charges Three Iran-Backed Operatives Over UK and European Plots

items.summary: At least 11 National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command workers died by suicide over roughly the past year, according to officials and public records, more than previously known. From early June to early July, five such deaths occurred, prompting a so-called suicide cluster designation. White House and congressional staff questioned agency leaders privately, while military commanders adjusted long work hours and expanded mental health support amid surging workloads tied to foreign conflicts.
items.title: Congress Scrutinizes Surge in NSA and Cyber Command Suicides

items.summary: Despite market bets on a de-escalation in the Iran war, new evidence has emerged of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and energy infrastructure. Crude prices hit two-month lows after U.S. officials downplayed further military action following Trump's conciliatory tone post-November 3 midterms. Yet attacks show little sign of abating: 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the war began, per the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.
items.title: Tankers Burn in Middle East Despite De-escalation Hopes

items.summary: The US dollar index closed near its highest level since October 28, up 0.5% after October consumer prices rose more than expected amid higher food and accommodation costs. Markets now price an 84% chance of a rate hike next month, with better-than-even odds for a January second hike.
items.title: Dollar Steady as Fed Hike Odds Rise on Hot Inflation Data

items.summary: Golf player Minjee Lee is expected to skip the LPGA Tour Championship in Naples from November 19-22, ending her difficult 2026 season. Her world ranking has fallen from third to 24th, described as her equal-lowest standing in 11 years. This would be her first absence from the event since 2014.
items.title: Minjee Lee set to miss Tour Championship after poor season

items.summary: Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer accused President Donald Trump of inaction after being briefed more than a year ago about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, whom US authorities identified as a suspected Chinese spy. Schumer posted on X that "Trump was briefed over A YEAR AGO" and "did nothing about it," while also criticizing the president for taking Huang to Beijing and accepting a $25 million donation from Nvidia. The allegations follow a New York Times report citing Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who reportedly reminded Trump again in May. Trump denied knowing about the relationship during his China visit but later defended Huang as an honorable man. An FBI probe and congressional review are underway.
items.title: Schumer Accuses Trump of Shielding Jensen Huang Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: Finshots explains that Indian companies are increasingly investing overseas, driving net foreign direct investment down from $43.9 billion to $6.7 billion in FY26 while outward flows rose from $18 billion to a record $49 billion over the same period. The outlet offers reasons for this trend—market access, acquiring capabilities and domestic spillovers—and notes that money leaving India can still bring value back through profits and exports. It also flags concerns about profit shifting, rupee pressure and round-tripping, concluding that the real question is whether these investments generate enough economic benefit at home.
items.title: India's Outward FDI Surges as Companies Invest Abroad

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love hit the stands on Tuesday, sparking political debates online and on television channels. However, contrary to expectations, the book contains few big revelations, focusing mostly on her life before politics. The period after 2004 is covered only in passing. Amitabh Bachchan's name appears just three times in the book, while his wife Jaya Bachchan is not mentioned at all. Political opponents like Lal Krishna Advani and Amit Shah are absent or briefly discussed. Sonia Gandhi recounts declining to become prime minister before Manmohan Singh, describing how alliance leaders pressured her until she mumbled 'Theek hai.' She also reflects on Indira Gandhi's early terrors in Parliament. The book acknowledges Emergency excesses while shifting some blame onto Sanjay and Maneka Gandhi.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi's memoir offers few surprises

items.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis defended the BJP-led Mahayuti government's decision to draft a Uniform Civil Code, citing constitutional Directive Principles of State Policy. He responded to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi's claim that the law was unconstitutional and Hindu-imposed. On the NCP merger question, he said neither Sharad Pawar nor Sunetra Pawar had informed him.
items.title: Maharashtra CM Defends UCC Draft Amid NCP Merger Speculation

items.summary: The release of Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, triggered a public dispute between the BJP and Congress over how it portrays Indian history. The BJP accused the book of whitewashing wrongs by the Nehru-Gandhi family, while Congress leaders countered that the ruling party was reviving old controversies ahead of Punjab elections. Opposing parties defended Gandhi's accounts, with PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti praising her as a stateswoman and Congress MP Pramod Tiwari calling the BJP's reaction a habit to benefit politically.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi memoir ignites BJP-Congress historical feud

items.summary: The Madras High Court ordered an FIR, freezing of bank accounts for Agal Vilakku Publication and proprietor Mohan, disciplinary action including suspension, and scrutiny of the amount spent on books. A Division Bench directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption to register the case immediately, per Press Trust of India. The court treated long-undebated allegations as unrebutted, citing repackaging of older works such as a 2013 book falsely presented as Kalki's work. It also referenced Jean Dreze denouncing another fake attribution at the Kalaignar Centenary Library in Madurai.
items.title: Madras HC Orders FIR and Account Freezes Over Fake Library Book Purchases

items.summary: In her newly released autobiography Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi recounts how 10-year-old Rahul relayed the news that his uncle Sanjay Gandhi had died in a plane crash on June 23, 1980. After receiving the message from RK Dhawan—"There has been an accident, Rahul. Chacha has died," Dhawan said—the boy repeated "Chacha e morto" while relaying it to his grandmother in Italy. The account also reflects on Italian as a family language and captures Indira Gandhi's grief over her son.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls Rahul relaying Sanjay's death

items.summary: Nvidia-backed CoreWeave said on Nov 10 it would reach adjusted profitability in the first half of 2028, reassuring investors as shares fell more than 40% over a month. The company cited strong demand and customer commitments backing its debt-fuelled expansion, with total debt around US$46.9 billion (S$60.09 billion) at end September. Chief executive Mike Intrator said customer contracts come first, and investment follows. Reuters.
items.title: CoreWeave Sets 2028 Profitability Goal Amid AI Bubble Fears

items.summary: A report alleges Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive, played a major role in moving restricted Nvidia AI chips into China and building links to China's Ministry of State Security. The Information identified companies centered on Shanghai Century Litong tied to Singapore-based Megaspeed. Separately, US intelligence suspects her involvement; previously Megaspeed was accused of helping China obtain around $2 billion worth of Nvidia processors.
items.title: Alice Huang Allegedly Helped Secure Nvidia AI Chip Imports

items.summary: On Tuesday OpenAI announced a beta called “Businesses” inside ChatGPT, letting companies claim and manage their profiles. The launch includes Business Hub for verified business details and product feeds plus aggregated insights on mentions, views and website clicks, and Business Agents to chat with company representatives. It is initially rolling out in the US to eligible e-commerce and online service businesses.
items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Businesses beta for US firms

items.summary: Jensen Huang, the 63-year-old chief of Nvidia, faces scrutiny after reports that he liaised with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive alleged to have aided Chinese intelligence. The fallout has triggered bipartisan calls for investigations on Capitol Hill, an internal review by Nvidia, and a Justice Department probe into whether Megaspeed violated export control laws. Nvidia's board said it had 'no reason to believe' that national security or company secrets were compromised, while Beijing dismissed the spy allegation as unsubstantiated. Huang apologized over the affair but did not address reports of Alice Huang being a suspected spy.
items.title: Nvidia CEO's affair and China ties draw probes

items.summary: WhatsApp CEO Kunal Shah said the platform will focus on making connections richer, letting users pay bills within chats, borrowing money or staying connected while travelling without extra steps, and using AI to improve efficiency. He stated personal messages and calls would stay end-to-end encrypted. In a post on X dated November 10, 2026, Shah said he spent months listening to users and described WhatsApp as “a shared language, spoken by 3bn+ people.” He noted the platform handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls daily. Meta appointed Shah in June; it also led a funding round of about ₹8,550 crore (about $900 million) in his fintech firm CRED.
items.title: WhatsApp CEO Kunal Shah Outlines Bill Payments and AI Focus

items.summary: Anthropic plans up to $64 billion (€57.1bn) in its US Securities and Exchange Commission filing, valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion (€1.25trn), below the prior $100 billion expectation. The week of November 16 listing would fall short of SpaceX's record raise. Analyst Art Hogan called it part of AI financing worries; Anthropic flags existential and regulatory risks.
items.title: Anthropic Sets $64 Billion IPO Below Record Valuations

items.summary: Reports suggest Apple could introduce OLED displays across both iPad Air models by the first quarter of 2027, with Samsung Display likely as main supplier. Industry estimates put combined shipments at 40-50 million units and iPad Pro at 30-40 million in 2027.
items.title: Apple may add OLED screens to iPad Air in 2027

items.summary: Anthropic unveiled a set of workplace productivity features at a company event, including Claude Sheets, which resembles Excel and Google Sheets but with Anthropic’s AI built in. The launch extends Claude beyond text generation into shared boards, spreadsheets and data stories available across paid plans on web, desktop and mobile. Anthropic said the tool reduced marketing reviews from three days to 24 hours. The company is positioning Claude as a platform where teams move from an idea to a working document while retaining context throughout.
items.title: Anthropic unveils AI work tools and takes on Microsoft

items.summary: In Washington, Microsoft and other companies and trade groups have pressed the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump to halt plans to bar imports from China of a key component used in artificial intelligence data centers, three people familiar with the situation said. The concern is that they could be used by Beijing to steal data, install malware or disrupt service at U.S. data centers.
items.title: Microsoft presses Trump to scuttle ban on Chinese data center tech

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive and a celebrated figure in Taiwan, is drawing mixed reactions after revelations of an affair with a woman possibly linked to Chinese intelligence. Both Nvidia's board and the FBI are investigating whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence efforts.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Scrutiny in Taiwan Over Alleged Spy Affair

items.summary: IBM is ending US visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division with more than 150,000 employees. Visa holders can keep working from abroad or leave the company by year-end; IBM has not said how many are affected. The decision follows years of declining high-skilled-visa use: H-1B petitions fell to just over 1,600 in fiscal year 2026 from more than 2,000 in FY2025 and nearly 3,000 in FY2024. IBM called it a business decision amid the Trump administration's push against foreign tech hiring.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa Sponsorship for Most Consultants

items.summary: WhatsApp CEO Kunal Shah said the platform will prioritize richer connections, task completion within chats like bill payments, and quietly integrating artificial intelligence while keeping personal messages and calls end-to-end encrypted. He noted WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls daily. Meta appointed CRED's founder in June after leading an Rs 8,550 crore funding round.
items.title: WhatsApp CEO Kunal Shah Outlines AI and Efficiency Focus While Preserving Encryption

items.summary: Jensen Huang's apology email addressed both Nvidia employees and his family amid reports of marital infidelity with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. The Wall Street Journal reported the affair. Nvidia launched an independent investigation into possible foreign intelligence involvement. Trump said the FBI was investigating. A shareholder sued over alleged investor deception.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Apology Email Sparks Investigation and Legal Action

items.summary: OpenAI announced it will discontinue the Advanced and Standard voice options in ChatGPT from December 11, moving users to its newer GPT-Live mode. The company said the change simplifies the voice experience while improving technology. Users currently using older modes will automatically switch after the date, though conversations remain available in history.
items.title: OpenAI Retires ChatGPT Voice Modes By December

items.summary: Google began rolling out Gemini 4 Carbon, which it calls its most capable model yet, to AI Mode in Google Search. Access is currently limited to paying Google AI Ultra subscribers. Robby Stein of Google said the model brings deeper reasoning and better instruction following, allowing longer conversations. Developers can use it via API at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. It targets harder queries while Auto and Fast options remain for everyday questions.
items.title: Google Rolls Out Gemini 4 Carbon To AI Mode

items.summary: On Nov 11 Asian equities diverged after renewed optimism over the AI trade was offset by forecast-topping October US inflation and talk of a larger December Federal Reserve hike. CoreWeave guidance, Anthropic’s planned IPO raise of up to US$64 billion valuing it at as much as US$1.4 trillion, and OpenAI quarterly revenue reaching US$10 billion lifted tech sentiment; Wall Street indexes fell on Nov 10. Chris Weston at Pepperstone said investors faced “no shortage of catalysts” amid the Democratic sweep, AI-infrastructure politics and a hotter-than-expected consumer price print.
items.title: Asian stocks waver as US rate fears temper tech rally

items.summary: A Goldman Sachs projection suggests Anthropic could generate about $685 billion in revenue by 2030, potentially ranking among the world's largest companies. The forecast coincides with preparations for a roughly $1.4 trillion IPO and plans to spend around $900 billion on AI development. The outlook raises questions amid an ongoing debate over AI safety.
items.title: Goldman Projects Anthropic Revenue Could Reach $685 Billion by 2030

items.summary: The unfolding Nvidia saga has intensified scrutiny over how top Chinese firms access advanced American compute. Megaspeed, suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, sits at the scandal's center. Meanwhile, legal export routes have created lucrative opportunities for Asian cloud operators serving Chinese hyperscalers like ByteDance and Moonshot, prompting a Carnegie Endowment expert to call the regime nonsensical.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Intensifies Scrutiny of Chip Export Loopholes

items.summary: On Tuesday, Spain's government demanded that TikTok suspend operations in the country until child sexual abuse material is eliminated, citing a media report documenting 1,183 explicit posts with millions of views. Youth Minister Sira Rego appealed to prosecutors and the Data Protection Agency for action, noting her ministry cannot ban the platform alone.
items.title: Spain Urges TikTok Suspension Over Abuse Content

items.summary: On November 10, OpenAI announced in beta within ChatGPT a feature called “Businesses” that lets companies claim and manage their profiles. Through Business Hub, verified businesses can update details and add product feeds with pricing and availability. Aggregated insights on mentions, views and website clicks are shown only above thresholds. Business Agents let users chat about products or services, and agents can be sponsored for ChatGPT Ads. The feature is initially rolling out to eligible e-commerce and online service businesses in the US.
items.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Businesses beta for US firms

items.summary: As world leaders gather for COP31 in Türkiye, the event’s focus on zero waste highlights how little material currently comes from recycled sources. NVIDIA presented four startups applying AI to improve recycling. AIRECO uses vision AI to sort plastics more finely toward closed-loop recycling, targeting nearly tripled capacity and an 85% cost cut next year. EverestLabs deploys about 150 robots that have identified roughly 40 billion objects. Greyparrot’s Analyzer operates in over 20 countries, cutting checks of tons of waste from 375 hours to six. reverse.fashion automates textile sorting with high-resolution computer vision.
items.title: NVIDIA Showcases AI Sorting Startups at COP31

items.summary: Adora Flora City departed Shanghai on November 9 for its first trial voyage, marking progress in China's homegrown cruise industry. The vessel and sister ship Adora Magic City berthed side by side at Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal on November 8. Testing will run through the voyage before Flora City begins operations on November 22. For the first three quarters of 2026, the port handled 55% of national cruise calls and 76% of passenger traffic, per Baoshan District People's government.
items.title: China's Two Homegrown Cruise Ships Berth Together in Shanghai

items.summary: A border trade fair in southwest China is gathering businesses from China and Vietnam, providing a platform for exploring new opportunities in trade and investment. As bilateral economic ties continue to grow, the event highlights the importance of cross-border connectivity and regional cooperation between the two countries.
items.title: Border Trade Fair Strengthens China-Vietnam Economic Ties

items.summary: On Tuesday OpenAI launched a beta Business Hub letting companies create verified business profiles, resembling Google's listings, plus specialized agents answering product questions. Benji Shomair, its VP of Monetization, said verification uses multiple methods across markets. The company noted ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI. This follows an earlier failed e-commerce push.
items.title: OpenAI launches business profiles and agent for ChatGPT

items.summary: In Haiyuan, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, ancient relics and new archaeological discoveries are shedding fresh light on the area's historical role as a crossroads of East–West trade. Once a bustling hub where civilizations converged, the region fostered artistic traditions, ingenuity and religious beliefs together. A thousand years later, its legacy still resonates across Haiyuan today. The article frames these findings within broader cultural exchange along the Silk Road. No figures or dates were provided in the item.
items.title: Haiyuan Revives Its Silk Road Legacy Through Archaeology

items.summary: For its 90th anniversary in 2026, CGTN Frontline produced 15 hand-drawn illustrations depicting the Long March through imagined letters from veterans. At China's Ministry of National Defense invitation, around 90 foreign military attachés from over 50 countries visited Guizhou and Sichuan provinces from November 2 to 7. Viewing the art and historic sites, they gained a deeper understanding of the march.
items.title: CGTN Frontline Illustrates Long March for Foreign Attachés

items.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang admitted cheating on his wife of 40 years, an affair that U.S. officials believe may involve national security concerns after Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was suspected of spying for China. The alleged spy reportedly helped build a network to acquire Nvidia chips, including Shanghai Century Litong, which facilitated $7.5 billion in purchases over two years, while Megaspeed bought $4.8 billion worth. Investigations by the U.S. and Singapore preceded the revelations, and Nvidia shares fell 5% after Huang's public apology on November 8, 2026. Trump defended him as a 'fine person,' while an independent board investigation began.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's Affair and China Spy Allegations

items.summary: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that people linked to the BJP, RSS and VHP oversaw the Ayodhya temple trust, construction, donations and bank deposits. He called for a wider investigation under Supreme Court supervision beyond the eight accused in the nearly 70,000-page SIT chargesheet, which named Avinash Shukla, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Yadav, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Subhash Srivastava and Tinnu. Investigators reportedly recovered Rs 79.85 lakh in cash from the accused except Srivastava and found 105 instances of unauthorised removal or concealment during counting. Ramesh also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the trust's formation on February 5, 2020.
items.title: Congress demands Supreme Court probe into Ram Temple donation embezzlement

items.summary: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar attacked Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, claiming the former chief minister would have prayers offered inside the Ram Mandir if his party won the 2027 assembly elections. Rajbhar said Yadav had earlier done so at Hanuman Garhi during his tenure between 2012 and 2017.
items.title: UP minister claims Akhilesh Yadav would offer namaz in Ram Mandir

items.summary: At the AI Engineer Code Summit, OpenAI hosted a workshop titled “New Ways of Working with Codex,” led by Developer Experience engineers Dominik Kundel and Charlie Guo. The session covered three themes: an awkward cloud transition that eased after version 2 was announced in late September; personal agents like dots and Anthropic's Claude Duet plus voice mode as new ways to steer coding tasks; and tips for using Codex. Kundel said the key is not getting too attached, since “things are constantly changing.” Attendees still find some cloud features confusing.
items.title: OpenAI Showcases New Ways of Working With Codex

items.summary: NVIDIA presents Alpamayo 2 Edge, an adaptive reasoning vision-language-action model built on a 2B Nemotron backbone and diffusion action expert. Post-trained with closed-loop reinforcement learning in AlpaGym, it improves closed-loop driving performance by 48.9% over the best non-closed-loop checkpoint while running at 160 ms to 190 ms latency on DRIVE AGX Thor.
items.title: NVIDIA Introduces Compact Reasoning Model for Onboard AV Use

items.summary: A shareholder sued Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang over an alleged failure to disclose the affair involving Alice Huang, suspected of working for Chinese intelligence. Filed Monday in California by Mark Kistenmacher, the complaint seeks unspecified damages amid reports that shares fell $7.97, or 4.3%, wiping out about $190 billion in value on Monday before declining again Tuesday. Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment (Source: AP).
items.title: Shareholder Lawsuit Targets Nvidia Over Spy-Affair Disclosure

items.summary: Raana Semiconductors Private Limited has signed a preorder agreement with SWELECT HHV Solar Photovoltaics Pvt. Ltd., a wholly owned subsidiary of SWELECT Energy Systems Ltd., for the supply of CZ12 ingot growers to support SHPV’s upcoming 1 GW ingot and wafer manufacturing facility in India.
items.title: Raana Semiconductors Signs CZ12 Ingot Grower Agreement for SWELECT’s Solar Facility

items.summary: Koh Puay Yang questions why the Ministry of Manpower has been quiet on foreign-worker quota abuses in massage establishments, which appear to rely heavily on Work Permit and S Pass holders. She notes Singapore's 35 per cent services-sector ceiling and asks how quotas are met when outlets lack local staff. The article cites phantom-worker disclosures from August 2023 and a May 2026 charge over false work-pass declarations, urging MOM to disclose investigations.
items.title: MP Calls for Scrutiny of Massage Industry Employment Rules

items.summary: Electricity bills in Jersey will increase by 2.5% from March 2027, announced by Jersey Electricity. The tariff change would add just over £1 a week for a typical all-electric home. Chief executive Chris Ambler said the company kept the rise below the island's inflation rate of 3%, which reached that level in September, and delayed it to avoid winter strain while investing £120m in network resilience.
items.title: Jersey electricity bills set to rise from March

items.summary: Aldi’s UK business is cutting hundreds of head office and logistics roles as part of a global effort to trim costs. The retailer consults its technology team on up to 150 roles after earlier redundancies, while store jobs remain unaffected. Aldi cites continuous operational review across its international business. It says it invested £300m in lowering prices on 900 products this year.
items.title: Aldi Trims UK Head Office and Logistics Roles Amid Cost Cuts

items.summary: A Kenyan domestic worker in Saudi Arabia reportedly received a sentence of 100 lashes after giving birth outside marriage, under sharia law that criminalises sex outside marriage. Rights groups condemned the punishment as an act of violence and said women are disproportionately targeted. The case surfaced because hospitals must report single mothers; many give birth at home unreported.
items.title: Kenyan Mother Sentenced in Saudi Arabia

items.summary: George Monbiot argues that Britain’s car manufacturers are resisting the transition to electric vehicles through lobbying and threats of investment withdrawal. As Cop31 opens, he says the government is expected to cut its zero-emission-car target from 80% by 2030 to about 60%. He blames moneyed influence over ministers for repeated concessions that allow hybrids and extend flexibilities to 2034. Citing BYD’s $10,000 Seagull versus unaffordable Western models, he says the industry is unfit for reality while governments dither.
items.title: Monbiot warns UK may weaken its EV target amid industry resistance

items.summary: The article asks why Australians do not stream Australian music, offering two possible reasons: live music is too costly and AI streaming algorithms dominate recommendations. It hedges these as likely causes without confirming them.
items.title: Australians Not Streaming Australian Music Explained

items.summary: The Guardian is reissuing a 2023 long-read podcast about computer scientist Joseph Weizenbaum, who helped create early artificial intelligence but came to reject it. Ben Tarnoff introduces the piece; Sam Peter Jackson reads it.
items.title: Weizenbaum's turn against AI from the Guardian archive

items.summary: Japan's largest oil refiner Eneos Holdings raised its fiscal 2026 net profit forecast by 48 per cent to 615 billion yen ($3.87 billion), citing stronger-than-expected oil prices, despite a renewable energy asset impairment of 111.8 billion yen in the July-September quarter.
items.title: Eneos Raises FY26 Profit Forecast on Oil Prices

items.summary: Hong Kong carrier Cathay Pacific said on Wednesday it exercised purchase rights for 14 more regional widebody and narrowbody Airbus aircraft as part of its fleet expansion and renewal plan. The orders include 11 Airbus A330-900 widebodies, bringing the total number of orders for the Airbus A330neo variants to 41, plus three additional Airbus A321neo jets beyond those ordered in 2023. CEO Ronald Lam said these new orders bring their total aircraft deliveries from 2026 to 120, closer to a plan of 150 new aircraft deliveries.
items.title: Cathay Pacific Exercises Purchase Rights for 14 Airbus Aircraft

items.summary: The Kennedy family has sued to stop construction of a triumphal arch President Donald Trump plans in the nation's capital, arguing it would obscure views of JFK's grave and thousands of veterans' burials at Arlington National Cemetery. A judge ordered a 14-day pause pending litigation. The White House called the suit unfortunate and said it is confident of vindication.
items.title: Kennedy family sues to block Trump arch near Arlington graves

items.summary: A federal judge removed Liam Bailey as liquidator of Hellyer Metals, which part-owned a north-west Tasmanian gold mine. Justice Shaun McElwaine said Bailey had failed to properly investigate the company's transactions and behaved in objectively concerning ways. Bailey was appointed on January 22, 2026, but did little investigative work before being removed Tuesday.
items.title: Federal judge removes Hellyer Metals liquidator amid failed deal

items.summary: Wild storms left thousands of homes without power across Western Australia's Midwest, Wheatbelt and Goldfields. In Mount Magnet the intense hail transformed the landscape into a white scene. Bureau of Meteorology meteorologist Dean Narramore said 30 millimetres fell in just 30 minutes.
items.title: WA hailstorm brings snow-like scene and power outages

items.summary: Ahead of European markets opening Wednesday, Asian stocks diverged as optimism over the AI trade was offset by forecast-topping US inflation data and expectations of a December rate hike. Beaten-down tech stocks bounced on bargain-buying after CoreWeave reported sales of $13-13.3 billion (€11.6-11.9bn) this year, beating estimates. Anthropic's planned IPO could raise up to $64 billion and value it at as much as $1.4 trillion. US consumer prices rose 0.4% month on month in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Fed officials signalled support for swift action. Oil edged higher amid hopes of a US-Iran deal. SoftBank tumbled up to 8% after reporting a loss of more than $7 billion (€6.24bn). Chris Weston of Pepperstone said there was no shortage of catalysts driving market price action.
items.title: Asian Stocks Diverge as US Rate Fears Temper Tech Bounce

items.summary: Sanjit Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College in Tilonia, Rajasthan, died on the morning of November 10. He was 81 and had spent more than five decades working to make rural communities self-reliant. The college he founded in 1972 said he passed away peacefully at home surrounded by family. Former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot praised his contributions to rural development, education and social work following Mahatma Gandhi's principles. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh described him as a pioneer institution builder who inspired many young people into social activism.
items.title: Barefoot College Founder Sanjit Bunker Roy Dies at 81

items.summary: President Nayib Bukele announced that El Salvador's military destroyed the headquarters of Haiti's largest crime gang, the 400 Mawozo. The ground and air attack targeted a complex on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince, reportedly in Croix-des-Bouquets. This is El Salvador's first military action against a Haitian target since deploying more than 2,000 soldiers last month to rescue four missing technicians. Bukele stated most gang members fled without fighting and posted video of helicopters firing on the complex. Some media outlets reported as many as 20 people were killed, but authorities have not confirmed this figure or the extent of damage.
items.title: El Salvador's military destroys Haitian gang headquarters

items.summary: According to the official mobile application developed by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Sirsa in Haryana recorded an air quality index of 403 at 7.05 am, placing it in the severe category and making it the most polluted northern city early Wednesday. Delhi logged an AQI of 299, classified as poor. Hisar ranked second with 377, followed by Baghpat (342) and Panchgaon (340). The concentration of highly polluted cities across Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi highlights the growing air quality challenge in northern India, renewing concerns over stricter enforcement of pollution-control measures.
items.title: Sirsa Hits Highest Northern AQI of 403 as Delhi Logs 299

items.summary: Muhammad Aminul Islam, Bangladesh's Chief Prosecutor of the International Crimes Tribunal, said Sheikh Hasina has no legal option but to face execution if she returns. He noted the appeal period for her November 2025 death sentence had expired and that tribunal law allows no further appeal or passport issuance.
items.title: Bangladesh Prosecutor Says Hasina Faces Execution If She Returns

items.summary: A liveblog reports that Ukraine and Russia began a second day of United States–mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi. Washington had called for a new security framework on the first day, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he was happy with changes in approach by US mediators. Negotiations are set to continue Wednesday.
items.title: Ukraine and Russia open second day of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi

items.summary: Pratiksha Tondwalkar of Pune rose from a part-time cleaner at the State Bank of India to assistant general manager. Born in 1964 into an economically disadvantaged family, she left school after Class 7 and married around age 19 or 20. In 1985 she was appointed a part-time cleaner earning about ₹60-65 a month, per News18. She resumed her education at night, scoring 60% in her Class 10 exam on the first attempt, and graduated in psychology. Appointed AGM at SBI in June 2022, she also studied naturopathy at 55 and supports disadvantaged children's education.
items.title: From Cleaner to Assistant General Manager at SBI

items.summary: A 17-year-old girl accused of helping her father, S Indushekar, kill seven family members in Bengaluru may face an adult trial. Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, a juvenile justice board must assess whether she understood and committed the heinous offences before deciding on transfer to the children’s court under Section 18(3). Investigators probe her role while forensic teams analyse evidence.
items.title: Juvenile Accused in Bengaluru Murders May Face Adult Trial

items.summary: Chief minister Joseph Vijay is scheduled to meet Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam legislators Wednesday at a hotel in Mahabalipuram, Chengalpattu district. The meeting follows opposition attacks on the party's first six months in office. Citing reports that over 10 crimes took place November 8 alone, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam alleged Tamil Nadu faced its worst period under TVK rule. Congress MP Karti P Chidambaram termed planned revenge killings alarming and worrisome.
items.title: Vijay meets TVK MLAs as government marks six months amid Opposition criticism

items.summary: A purported video shows RJD MLA Naresh Prasad Singh riding on a man's shoulders to cross a river in Palamu district, Jharkhand. The carried man, identified as belonging to the Dalit community, lost his balance and fell into the water midway while the MLA landed unsteadily but upright. The clip has triggered political and social controversy.
items.title: RJD MLA Piggybacking on Dalit Man Sparks Controversy in Jharkhand

items.summary: An Aam Aadmi Party–BJP dispute has emerged over post-Diwali air pollution and air quality index data in Delhi NCR. The party cited data suggesting stubble burning in Punjab had little impact on Delhi's smog, alleging removal of the website displaying it and manipulation of Diwali-night figures after extreme particulate spikes were reported. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa denied these claims.
items.title: Aam Aadmi Party and BJP clash over Delhi air pollution data

items.summary: At least six new vehicles launched this year seek more than $1.25 billion for real estate and infrastructure assets, marking a resurgence after slow growth. The shift follows Indian equities losing momentum: the Nifty 50 delivered just 7% over two years versus 29% in the S&P 500. Firms such as Neo Wealth and EAAA India Alternatives Ltd. report large raises for real-asset funds, while Julius Baer and EY India note family offices now allocate roughly half their portfolios to alternatives.
items.title: Indian family offices pivot capital toward real estate and infrastructure

items.summary: Brent futures rose 71 cents, or 0.78%, to $92.20 a barrel by 0119 GMT, while WTI crude gained 49 cents, or 0.57%, to $86.53. The gains followed reports that 37 ships were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waterways in October, per the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, with 10 attacks recorded so far this month.
items.title: Oil climbs as Hormuz attacks outweigh Iran truce hopes

items.summary: New research published in Science indicates more than 40% of terrestrial vertebrates could lose part of their habitat to sea level rise by the end of the century. The study overlaid suitability maps for roughly 34,120 species with five IPCC scenarios and found reptiles especially vulnerable; between 14,325 and 15,324 species would be exposed by 2100. Losses concentrate in the Amazon delta and Southeast Asia, where refugia often lie outside protected areas.
