Co-author Zhong-Wen Jiang stresses that mitigation alone will not protect remaining habitats. The authors note their estimates are conservative and exclude marine zones.
items.title: Sea Rise Threatens Most Land Vertebrates Worldwide

items.summary: South Korean chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK hynix could face tighter export compliance requirements if US authorities increase scrutiny of Nvidia’s AI chip shipments to China, following reports that CEO Jensen Huang had a personal relationship with Alice Huang, suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. No new restrictions have been announced; the investigation into Megaspeed began in 2024 and remains unproven. Stricter checks could raise compliance costs for high-bandwidth memory suppliers, though diversification toward proprietary AI processors may create offsetting opportunities. Nvidia’s board expressed confidence that no secrets were compromised, while Vice Science Minister Ryu Je-myung said GPU deliveries are expected to proceed without disruption.
items.title: Nvidia Scandal Raises Export Risks for South Korean Chipmakers

items.summary: A report by The Information alleges that Alice Huang, Jensen Huang's alleged mistress and suspected intelligence operative, used her ties to route advanced Nvidia chips into China. According to figures cited in the report, Megaspeed International and its Malaysia-linked company Speedmatrix imported or routed chips worth a combined $6.6 billion, while the wider network totalled approximately $7.5 billion across roughly 240,000 processors including H100 and H200 systems. The allegations unfold against Washington's export controls on advanced semiconductors to China.
items.title: Report Alleges Alice Huang Diverted Nvidia Chips to China

items.summary: Procurement records show Northwestern Polytechnical University bought two H200 AI chips last month for 874,700 yuan ($123,000), despite being on the US export blacklist since 2001. The university is part of China's "Seven Sons of National Defense" group and conducts military research in Xian. Reuters reports the purchases for the first time, noting gaps in Washington's efforts to curb advanced technology access. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over lobbying for looser chip sales restrictions. Northwestern Polytechnical also secured computing contracts through domestic suppliers, including servers with A100 and A800 chips banned from export.
items.title: Blacklisted Chinese University Bought Nvidia Chips Despite US Ban

items.summary: Anthropic announced updated versions of its Fable and Mythos AI models, which the company said can run up to 30% faster on complex tasks while costing 20% less. The launches coincide with an initial public offering expected for the week of November 16, when it is anticipated to raise as much as $100 billion.
items.title: Anthropic Unveils Faster Models Ahead of Record IPO

items.summary: Nvidia hired former prosecutor Joon Kim and his firm Wachtell Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate CEO Jensen Huang’s suspected relationship with a Chinese spy. Around $430bn was wiped off its value as shares fell nearly 5.5% on Monday after a 4.27% drop the prior day.
items.title: Nvidia Hires Law Firm After Spy Allegations Erode Its Value

items.summary: CNA analysts say alleged spying allegations involving Nvidia's CEO could prompt tougher US enforcement of advanced chip export restrictions, with cloud providers and trading hubs in Southeast Asia facing greater scrutiny. Alex Capri calls such services a long-standing loophole and expects Washington to focus on neocloud companies, while Malaysia recently seized 30 servers worth about US$12.1 million at Kuala Lumpur International Airport during suspected smuggling. Jay Goldberg of Seaport Research Partners says rival chipmakers could benefit as demand for Nvidia's products remains strong; he also notes leadership uncertainty after shares fell more than 5 per cent.
items.title: Analysts Warn Jensen Huang Scandal May Tighten AI Chip Scrutiny in Southeast Asia

items.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) reports that capacity utilisation at compressed biogas plants in India is low, around 35 per cent, citing difficulties procuring adequate feedstock. The agency notes new projects consolidated in the central Gobardhan registry show promising accelerated growth and expects exponential CBG production growth by 2031 if new plants operate comparably with existing facilities.
items.title: IEA Reports Low CBG Plant Utilisation in India

items.summary: Tata Consultancy Services became the Official AI and Technology Partner of the Rio Marathon, its first marathon sponsorship in Latin America. TCS plans to deploy artificial intelligence, data analytics, and digital innovation capabilities at the event. The 2026 edition registered approximately 70,000 runners across four distances in 2026, generating a record economic impact of R$ 711 million for Rio de Janeiro. Meanwhile, TCS stock fell 0.81 per cent to ₹2,455.40 by early afternoon trade.
items.title: TCS Signs Rio Marathon Tech Deal Amid Stock Slump

items.summary: Huawei has launched the Luterra S2, an all-in-one residential energy storage system combining a hybrid inverter, lithium iron phosphate batteries and AI-based energy management. Single-phase inverters are rated from 3 kW to 10 kW; three-phase units run from 5 kW to 20 kW, with up to three 20 kW inverters paralleled for 60 kW combined output. Battery modules offer usable capacities of 4. 9 kWh and 6. 9 kWh, scaling to a maximum nominal storage capacity of 336 kWh across up to 48 packs.
items.title: Huawei Launches All-in-One Residential Energy Storage System

items.summary: OpenAI's operating losses widened to $10.9 billion (€9.72bn) from $10.1 billion, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. Its quarterly revenue rose about 50% to $10 billion in the third quarter, and its adjusted operating margin improved to -109% from -150%. The disclosure comes as investors scrutinise AI finances amid Anthropic's planned IPO.
items.title: OpenAI Posts Steep Losses Amid Revenue Rise

items.summary: A New York Times investigation reportedly suggests Nvidia may have targeted its CEO in a suspected intelligence operation involving advanced AI chips. The allegations centre on Singapore-based Megaspeed, Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang. Questions remain about corporate structures and information transfer to Beijing amid broader concerns over technology security.
items.title: Nvidia Faces Allegations of China Espionage Over Jensen Huang

items.summary: SBI Research forecasts Indian economic activity could expand at an annualised rate of 7.8% in the September quarter, above the Reserve Bank of India's estimate of 7.2%. Moody's Ratings separately raised its full-year FY27 growth forecast to 7%, citing resilient consumption and improving investment. SBI Research's November 11 report describes economic activity as robust during July–September 2026.
items.title: SBI Research Forecasts India's GDP Growth Above RBI Projection

items.summary: Juliane Koepcke, now 71, recounts surviving the Christmas Eve 1971 crash of LANSA Flight 508 over Peru. At 17 she was one of 92 aboard; ninety-one died and up to 14 later succumbed before rescue. She fell thousands of metres into the rainforest alone and wandered for ten days, aided by her parents’ research station just 30 miles away. Koepcke told the BBC about seeing a bright light on the engine and hearing calm words from her mother before the plane broke apart. On day ten she treated an infested wound with petrol from wreckage debris until rescuers found her. She was the only passenger to walk out of the jungle alive.
items.title: Amazon Crash Survivor Recalls Eleven-Day Jungle Rescue

items.summary: Microsoft has sent a warning to the White House that US data centres could halt if the FCC’s proposed import ban on Chinese optical transceivers is passed. The software company, building 35 data centers and planning 134 more, reportedly met with science and security officials recently. ITI executive John Miller said the chips “could just sit there waiting around unutilized.” A Tom’s Hardware report notes concerns that China-made components could be compromised to steal data or disrupt American facilities.
items.title: Microsoft Warns US Over China Optical Transceiver Ban

items.summary: The New York Times reported that President Trump was briefed aboard Air Force One in May about intelligence suggesting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was involved with a suspected Chinese spy, contradicting his claim of knowing nothing during his Beijing visit. Secretary Marco Rubio delivered the briefing shortly before Huang joined the delegation at Trump’s invitation. China rejected claims Alice Huang, not related to the CEO, was a spy.
items.title: Trump Briefed on Nvidia Chief’s Ties to Alleged Chinese Spy

items.summary: Microsoft fixed sign-in and mail delivery problems on Exchange Server systems after installing the October 2026 Windows Server security updates. The issues, acknowledged in mid-October, stemmed from a new default memory limit for Endpoint Mapper handling Endpoint Lookup calls. Microsoft said some servers may never be affected and urged customers not to uninstall the OWA-related update; November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates (KB5131080 and KB5131090) address it, with a registry-key workaround available.
items.title: Microsoft Patches Outlook Sign-In Breaks From Windows Server Updates

items.summary: Nvidia’s stock fell about 9.5% over two days with little news, even after the board hired Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate a suspected affair between Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, whom intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. Corporate governance professors Ann Lipton of the University of Colorado and Todd Henderson of the University of Chicago say there is no real precedent. The board said it has “no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised.” Nvidia owns about 3.6% voting control, which both experts note makes Huang easier to dislodge than a dual-class structure would allow.
items.title: Nvidia Board Hires Counsel as Stock Slides on CEO Scandal

items.summary: Anthropic unveiled office tools including a video call assistant, data dashboard tool and Claude Sheets ahead of its public listing. Nicholas Lin called the spreadsheet experience “fairly basic,” aimed at paid users rather than advanced work like financial modeling. Anthropic seeks about $1.4 trillion valuation as sales surge.
items.title: Anthropic Launches Office Tools Ahead of IPO and Faces Microsoft Rivalry

items.summary: WhatsApp's new global head Kunal Shah said the platform will add bill payments, money borrowing and other task features to chats, alongside richer voice notes, stickers and video and quietly useful artificial intelligence. He noted WhatsApp handles over 100 billion messages and 2 billion calls daily while keeping personal messages end-to-end encrypted. Meta appointed him in June after leading a funding round of about Rs 8,550 crore (about USD 900 million) in fintech platform CRED.
items.title: WhatsApp CEO Kunal Shah Announces Bill Payments and AI Tools

items.summary: On her 91st birthday, Google Arts & Culture launched the first online retrospective of artist Dr. Esther Mahlangu’s work, offering more than 45 stories and a rich archive to a global audience. The project combined curatorial research with AI from Google DeepMind and Domestic Data Streamers’ synthetic memories initiative to recreate her undocumented early life, including moments before 1980 that were previously missing. More than 45 exhibitions across institutions tell how she became known in the world.
items.title: Google Honors Dr. Esther Mahlangu With Online Retrospective

items.summary: Benjamin Guin of the Bank’s Strategy and Policy Approach Division argues that AI makes producing polished, well-structured analysis cheaper and faster, widening a gap between abundant evidence supply and scarce accountable attention. He illustrates this with Chart 1 as two scissors blades: falling production cost versus flatter accountable capacity. The article notes controlled studies find productivity gains of 25% to 40%, that UK financial services firms using AI rose from 58% in 2022 to 86% by the Bank of England and Financial Conduct Authority’s 2026 survey, and cites Canada’s national consultation drawing over 11,300 respondents. Guin concludes institutions’ comparative advantage may shift toward verifying evidence rather than producing it.
items.title: AI lowers analysis costs while accountability stays fixed

items.summary: The SEC asked a Manhattan federal judge to close the investor Fair Fund created after Elon Musk settled its 2018 securities-fraud case over an August 7, 2018 tweet. Musk and Tesla each paid $20 million in fines for alleged fraud without admitting wrongdoing; neither defendant admitted fault. The SEC said distribution of the fund is now complete.
items.title: SEC Seeks Closure of Musk–Tesla Fair Fund

items.summary: In a noon news digest, Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, led by ex-prosecutor Joon Kim, to investigate whether its chief executive has any link with an alleged Chinese spy. Separately, Indian stock markets rallied on Wednesday, with Sensex surging over 1,350 points and Nifty crossing 25,400 to reach eight-month highs.
items.title: Nvidia Hires Law Firm To Probe CEO Jensen

items.summary: A highly classified memo warned US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, an individual suspected of operating as a Chinese intelligence asset. The White House dismissed the reporting, while China called it groundless speculation. Officials briefed congressional leaders on Monday.
items.title: Classified Memo Raises National Security Concerns Over Nvidia CEO's Alleged Chinese Links

items.summary: Singapore's accountancy sector added jobs and raised median salaries across all surveyed seniority levels in 2025, according to the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority's Accounting Entities Survey. The workforce grew by 579 positions, or 2.7%, from 21,783 in 2024 to 22,362 in 2025, while revenue rose 5.1% to about $3.7 billion. Acting Minister for Manpower Jasmin Lau said firms must help young accountants develop judgment as routine tasks are automated, and noted that reconciliations and first drafts—traditionally how juniors learn—are now partly handled by AI. The sector is prioritising new skills like AI application and ethics.
items.title: Singapore Accountancy Sector Adds Jobs and Raises Pay Amid AI Shift

items.summary: CGTN and Euronews launch Crossing Cultures, a five-part series co-produced by the two outlets that explores AI glasses and their privacy questions. In Shenzhen reporter Yang Zhao tests real-time translation with an Australian visitor while Euronews reporter Denis Loctier meets deaf Liu Shanshan trying speech-to-caption glasses.
items.title: AI Glasses Offer Real-Time Translation in New Series

items.summary: In remarks dated November 10, 2026 at the Council on Foreign Relations, Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman reviewed her outlook for the U.S. economy. She noted real GDP likely rose more than 3 percent in the third quarter after a solid 2.4 percent pace earlier this year, while unemployment edged down to 4.1 percent in October and monthly job gains averaged about 80,000 through October. Bowman said progress on lowering inflation has disappointed; today's consumer price index suggests 12-month core PCE inflation likely moved up further to 3.3 percent in October. She forecast that as shocks wane or unwind with no labor-market pressures emerging, core PCE inflation will move closer to 2 percent next year. Bowman emphasized monitoring energy markets and the AI buildout, warning of risks from equity corrections and rising financing costs if AI revenues fall short.
items.title: Bowman Outlines Fed Policy Outlook Amid AI and Energy Pressures

items.summary: According to a filing with the exchange, HEG Advanced Materials said its TACC subsidiary secured an Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) incentive for its Synthetic Graphite Anode Material project at Sirsoda Industrial Area, Dewas, Madhya Pradesh. The facility spans more than 100 acres and targets capacity beyond 30,000 metric tonnes per annum by FY2028-29, with a first phase of 20,000 MTPA aimed for commissioning by June 2027. Chairman Riju Jhunjhunwala thanked the Government of India and the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology. The company also reported Q2FY27 revenue of Rs 429.94 crore and profit after tax of Rs 208.89 crore, while shares gained over 4% in a week.
items.title: HEG shares rise after subsidiary wins Rs 610 crore incentive

items.summary: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari on Wednesday criticised Trinamool Congress MP Kirti Azad over his remarks on Lord Ram and the Ayodhya Ram Mandir, accusing the opposition of “peak vote bank politics”. He warned that opposition parties would face punishment in the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, similar to the TMC’s electoral defeat in West Bengal. The report was written by Pranjal Pandey for The Times of India.
items.title: BJP Targets Kirti Azad Over Ram Mandir Remarks

items.summary: BJP Rajya Sabha member Sudhanshu Trivedi criticised Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, claiming she gave up the Prime Minister's post in 2004 but became chairperson of the National Advisory Council (NAC) with Cabinet minister rank. He said “She gave up the post of Prime Minister and became a Super PM.” His remarks follow her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love.
items.title: BJP Accuses Sonia Gandhi of Being a Super PM

items.summary: Wang Yi met Slovak Foreign Minister Juraj Blanár in Beijing on Tuesday, the two sides said. Wang said China is ready to strengthen political mutual trust with Slovakia and jointly uphold trade liberalization and economic globalization, while expressing hope that Slovakia would continue a constructive role in China-Europe relations. Blanár said Slovakia opposes protectionism and trade wars.
items.title: Chinese and Slovak Foreign Ministers Meet in Beijing

items.summary: Meta announced on Monday that its AI agent, Muse, is now available on the Apple Watch and Android’s Wear OS. Users can interact with it through voice calls, text messages or dictation directly from their smartwatch. The launch follows a dedicated iPad app introduced in September. Shortly after launching, Muse became one of just 12 mobile apps to surpass 10 million U.S. downloads within their first 40 days in the App Store.
items.title: Meta Expands Its AI Agent Muse to Apple Watch and Android Wear OS

items.summary: George Yeo, former foreign minister of Singapore and an APEC founding participant from 1989, revisits the organisation's original purpose: keeping economies across the Pacific united. In this episode of The Power of Ideas he argues that differences in political systems and development paths need not prevent economies from trading, cooperating and learning from one another, and considers what opportunities Shenzhen's meeting may bring.
items.title: Former Singapore Foreign Minister George Yeo on APEC's role in a multipolar world

items.summary: The article argues that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has lost the argument for keeping US chip sales open to China, following revelations he had an affair with a woman alleged by US intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Hawks in Washington have seized on the disclosure to press for stricter controls on technology transfers, dismissing his advocacy as self-serving and absurd. Under Xi Jinping, Beijing is pursuing tech self-sufficiency while strictly limiting imports of Nvidia’s H200 chips despite Trump greenlighting them. Huang hired crisis communications firm Heller around October 2025 after being linked to Alice Huang. Senator Chris Coons called the administration “corrupt,” and Thompson concluded that “he has only himself to blame.” The piece asserts significant commercial consequences for Nvidia.
items.title: Jensen Huang loses China chip sales debate amid spy scandal

items.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Tesla’s robotaxi service has begun operating in San Antonio, citing Axios and a Tesla Robotaxi account post. The service currently covers downtown and nearby areas but does not reach the airport, unlike Waymo’s robotaxi service there. It remains unclear how many vehicles are active.
items.title: Tesla Robotaxi Service Expands Into San Antonio

items.summary: Jonathan Ross said he is “as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation”, adding that he was “genuinely unaware of their conduct”. The Guardian and ITV News published allegations against Walliams, 55, after a court rejected his attempt to block them; he denies wrongdoing. Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said she would meet industry members to “draw a line in the sand” over abuse. Jess Phillips urged that the law intervene so such claims are not silenced. Walliams has been dropped by Independent Talent Group and suspended from Labour, while broadcasters review or remove his programmes.
items.title: Jonathan Ross Reacts to Walliams and Brand Revelations

items.summary: Andy Burnham welcomed government announcements approving the next stage of two offshore wind projects, RWE and KKR’s £12bn Vanguard West and East scheme—believed to be the biggest of its kind in UK history—and Scottish-headquartered SSE’s Berwick Bank B phase. The schemes will support 2,400 jobs and 2,677 skilled roles respectively; offshore construction is set for early 2027, with operational targets by 2030. Burnham said the investment makes “power under British control.”
items.title: Burnham welcomes approval for two UK windfarm projects

items.summary: Congo's government said Wednesday the country's deadliest Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, with 5,387 deaths — nearly half of those infected. The Bundibugyo virus spread to eight of Congo's 26 provinces since being declared in mid-May. Armed conflict, a health system crisis and violence against workers hinder containment efforts.
items.title: Congo's Deadliest Ebola Outbreak Surpasses 11,000 Cases

items.summary: At the launch of the IIAG, Mo Ibrahim argued that Africa’s average governance score rose only 0.8 points between 2016 and 2025 to 50.1 out of 100, while security and rule of law fell by 1.7 despite gains in economic opportunity (3.7) and human development (2.5). The index draws on 51 sources across 54 countries over ten years. Nathalie Delapalme warned that without security and the rule of law, progress is fragile. Ibrahim said “the buck stops here” with post-independence governments, while cautioning against ignoring international arrangements draining resources from Africa.
items.title: Africa's governance gains narrow as rule of law slips

items.summary: Private-sector members of Japan's Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy said Wednesday that hitting the central bank's 2 per cent inflation target is not an end in itself, stressing higher incomes and productivity were needed for lasting progress. The core consumer price index rose an annual 2.1 per cent in September, exceeding the Bank of Japan target for the first time in nine months.
items.title: Japan economic panel urges sustained growth focus after inflation target met

items.summary: The Supreme Court ruled Wednesday that the July 2025 Upper House election was conducted in an “unconstitutional state” due to vote-value disparities of up to 3.13, yet dismissed requests to invalidate it. The ruling passed 10 of 15 justices.
items.title: Japan's Supreme Court Upholds July 2025 Upper House Election

items.summary: Japan marked the 40th anniversary of its flagship international exchange program this month, celebrating four decades since JET launched in 1987 to promote foreign-language education and grassroots cultural exchanges. The initiative grew from an initial 848 participants into one of the world’s largest such programs. However, it now faces mounting pressure as translation work declines amid artificial intelligence proliferation and a weak yen reduces its appeal.
items.title: JET Programme Turns 40 Amid AI and Yen Pressures

items.summary: The US warned Madagascar against strengthening its ties with Russia, citing failed partnerships with West African militaries that have not improved security. Africa Command's Lt Gen John Brennan said the region is vital to global trade and cautioned against what he called the 'Sahel model'. President Michaël Randrianirina has reiterated support for stronger Russian links; Madagascar and Russia signed cooperation agreements last month, marking a first official visit by a Malagasy leader in 50 years.
items.title: US warns Madagascar over deepening military ties with Russia

items.summary: Indonesian investigators expect further developments after sentencing Tonny Tumbelaka to nine years for arranging a shipment of more than 3 metric tons of pangolins scales found at Tanjung Priok port. Customs officials uncovered the consignment, valued at $10.1 million, concealed among sea cucumbers and instant noodles en route to Cambodia in February this year.
items.title: Indonesia Convicts Man in Major Pangolin Trafficking Case

items.summary: After roughly three years on the road and selling just over 20,000 units last year against a projected 250,000 vehicles annually, Tesla announced that Elon Musk would wind down Cybertruck production next year to make room for Cybercabs. The article frames the truck as one of the most polarizing flops in automotive history and notes rising prices — its starting price was raised to $92,500 — alongside a partisan divide over EVs. Advocates like Dan Krassner argue cheaper models are coming and that Republican resistance is easing, suggesting America’s electrified pickup experiment isn’t over yet.
items.title: Tesla Plans Cybertruck Production Winddown for Cybercabs

items.summary: After Democrats won every statewide race in Georgia last week, including two Public Service Commission seats ending a 30-year Republican majority (quantity-393-401), the new Democratic commissioners say their top priority is reinining rising electricity bills from Georgia Power. They plan to challenge plans approved in December 2025 for nearly 10 gigawatts of gas-fired capacity serving proposed data centers, which critics estimate could cost customers $50 billion to $60 billion over decades (quantity-867-879). Edwards said “Georgia Power is making billions while Georgia families are struggling” during an Oct. 28 press event hosted by the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy.
items.title: Georgia regulators plan to curb Georgia Power’s gas buildout

items.summary: England’s higher education regulator says AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework, prompting calls for a return to traditional exams and in-person presentations after lecturers complained. The Office for Students (OfS) said degree credibility is under threat from widespread AI use in essays and open-book exams. Josh Fleming called it a generational risk. A report by the OfS and Advance HE interviewed more than 300 students and staff at 127 universities this year.
items.title: Regulator warns AI undermines university grading

items.summary: SA Health confirmed a young adult died from invasive meningococcal disease, the state's health minister and chief public health officer having confirmed the case on Saturday, October 31. SA Health said confidentiality prevented further details; no additional cases have been reported, with the deceased the 22nd such case in South Australia this year.
items.title: Young adult dies from meningococcal disease

items.summary: La Banque africaine de développement (BAD), sous la direction de son président Sidi Ould Tah, qui a pris ses fonctions en 2025, promeut une nouvelle architecture financière pour réduire la dépendance à l'égard des financements extérieurs. L'article décrit un cadre commun visant à réorganiser la mobilisation et le déploiement des capitaux africains, soutenu par le sommet de l'Union africaine en février 2026. La banque a renforcé son engagement auprès d'institutions régionales, comme une ligne de crédit de 70 millions de dollars américains versée à la Banque de développement des États de l'Afrique centrale. Une initiative prévoit un programme de capital hybride démarrant d'ici fin 2026.
items.title: BAD prône une nouvelle architecture du financement en Afrique

items.summary: At least three Central Reserve Police Force personnel were injured after terrorists opened fire on them Wednesday in the Kulgam district of Kashmir Valley. The incident is described as a terror attack, with no further details provided about casualties or the attackers' identity.
items.title: Three CRPF Personnel Injured in Kulgam Attack

items.summary: US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks entered their second day in Abu Dhabi, with Zelenskyy welcoming a shift in Washington's approach while noting no breakthrough. Divisions persist over territory, security guarantees and ceasefire terms. Kushner said gaps narrowed; Lavrov dismissed European involvement. The sides consider exchanging 1,000 prisoners each, possibly 1,500.
items.title: Ukraine-Russia Peace Talks Enter Second Day Over Territory and Security

items.summary: The Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority is investigating after its website was hacked during the exam period, a VCAA spokesperson confirmed in a statement. The home page showed an error message replaced with "We'll be right back." A forensic investigation is underway to determine the attack's extent. There is no indication that exam papers from today or previous weeks have been accessed, and exams run through November 18.
items.title: VCAA Investigates Website Hack During Exam Period

items.summary: On Tuesday, Delhi Water Minister Parvesh Verma rode a jet ski on the Yamuna at the launch of Namo Yamuna River Safari, the city's first cruise service. Verma said the BJP government has taken significant steps toward rejuvenation work along the 52-km Yamuna stretch through Delhi over the past 18 months. The electric vessel carries about 30 passengers on a journey lasting roughly 45 minutes for ₹500, with entry to the riverfront premises at ₹50. The terminal sits at Sonia Vihar near Jagatpur. A second cruise is planned by February-March 2027.
items.title: Delhi Launches First Yamuna River Cruise With Jet Ski Ride

items.summary: Anna, a Chinese teacher and content creator from Russia, shares her life in Wenzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province. She shows viewers experiences of local intangible cultural heritage and time spent with family through personal stories that give audiences abroad a glimpse of China through her eyes. Such intermingling of cultures and people-to-people exchanges are another way APEC brings the region closer.
items.title: Russian creator films daily life in China's Wenzhou for APEC

items.summary: A seven-year study by the Phnom Penh-based company Fishing Cat Ecological Enterprise found that Cambodia’s mangrove forests and associated wetlands provide critical refuge for threatened species such as fishing cats and hairy-nosed otters. Researchers deployed camera traps across 156 coastal and riverine sites between 2017 and 2023 in the Peam Krasop Wildlife Sanctuary and adjacent Koh Kapik Ramsar site, Cambodia’s largest mangrove expanse. Corresponding author Vanessa Herranz Muñoz said protecting both forests is essential for species like the large-spotted civet.
items.title: Study Finds Cambodia’s Mangroves Shelter Threatened Wildlife

items.summary: Researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and Dalian Jiaotong University built a small methylammonium-free perovskite solar module with an active area of 54.80 cm, reaching efficiency of 22.7%. They used slot-die coating under ambient conditions plus rubidium thiocyanate and formamidinium thiocyanate additives to widen the crystallization processing window beyond 100 seconds. The result beat a reference module without those additives by more than ten percentage points.
items.title: Chinese Researchers Build Methylammonium-Free Perovskite Solar Module Reaching 22.7% Efficiency

items.summary: An Israeli drone strike killed Hani al-Khudari, 44, on the rooftop of his home near Sheikh Radwan Cemetery in western Gaza City. Medical sources told Anadolu Agency that he was targeted while filling water when a missile struck him Wednesday, killing him and injuring several others taken to Al-Shifa Hospital. The attack occurred amid continued Israeli violations of the ceasefire agreement, which took effect Oct. 10, 2025.
items.title: Israeli Drone Strike Kills Palestinian in Gaza City

items.summary: A UN Women briefing says AI is worsening online abuse against women in the Middle East, by spreading disinformation and image-based or deepfake content. Around 68% of regional women report dealing with technology-facilitated gender-based violence, versus roughly a global average of 40-65%, while nearly all have seen it online; about half feel unsafe online, rising to almost 70% among visible activists and journalists. A World Bank briefing notes honor norms can turn digital abuse into real-world consequences.
items.title: AI tools intensify online harassment of Middle East women

items.summary: This excerpt from Deep Human by Crystal Lim-Lange and Gregor Lim-Lange offers tips for engaging in mindful conversations at work, starting with identifying whom you are speaking to. The authors suggest assessing whether a person leans toward the relationship or task end of a spectrum, noting that relationship-focused people prefer emotional appeals while task-focused individuals value structure and data. They reference a study finding judges had a 65% chance of favourable rulings in the morning and again after lunch breaks. The book also draws on Marshall Rosenberg’s teaching about universal human needs to avoid conflict standoffs.
items.title: A self-help book on mindful workplace conversations

items.summary: The Gauhati High Court held that Permanent Account Number cards and voter ID cards alone cannot establish Indian citizenship unless supported by the records used to issue them. The ruling came while dismissing Kulchan Begum’s petition challenging a Foreigners Tribunal order declaring her a foreigner who entered India in March 1971, upholding the tribunal decision and revoking her interim bail.
items.title: Gauhati High Court Rejects PAN and Voter ID as Proof of Citizenship

items.summary: Israeli Ambassador Reuven Azar told the India Today Group's Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference in New Delhi that agrivoltaics could let farmers grow crops and generate solar electricity on the same land. He warned that expanding solar farms might divert agricultural land, threatening food security within a decade. Azar said Israel has developed technology allowing more than 50 crops to be grown alongside panels, though he noted affordability remains too expensive for small farmers.
items.title: Israel Envoy Proposes Agrivoltaics for Indian Farms

items.summary: Three Central Reserve Police Force personnel were injured after terrorists opened fire on a checkpoint in Jammu and Kashmir's Kulgam district. The attackers arrived on motorcycles, leaving two jawans seriously hurt before security forces retaliated and launched counter operations to track them down.
items.title: Three CRPF Jawans Injured in Terrorist Fire in Kulgam

items.summary: The Straits Times reports that Swiftdata, the parent of Megaspeed International at the centre of US and Singapore investigations into possible diversion of advanced Nvidia chips to China, lists a Midview City unit it did not appear to occupy when visited on Nov 11. Tenants say an interior design firm has occupied the address for over four years; its co-founder says he leased directly from Midview City and never heard of Swiftdata or Megaspeed. Complex manager Philip Chang declined comment citing PDPA regulations, while Nvidia chief Jensen Huang called the dealings “normal and not unusual.”
items.title: Singapore firm's registered address occupied by interior design company amid Nvidia chip probe

items.summary: IBM describes technical advances toward its planned fault-tolerant quantum computer, IBM Quantum Starling, slated for 2029. The framework was detailed in a 2025 paper introducing bivariate bicycle qLDPC error correction codes that cut resource needs by about 10x physical qubits. Progress spans device physics on Loon and Heron/Nighthawk processors, decoder improvements via Relay-BP, inter-module l-couplers linking Nighthawk processors, a new modular cryogenic design, and ASICs matching room-temperature control performance. IBM notes Starling remains years away but that the chosen pathway has been validated.
items.title: IBM Reports Progress Toward Fault-Tolerant Quantum Starling

items.summary: The Finnish embassy in Canberra was temporarily closed on Tuesday, 10 November 2026 for an innocuous staff training day. Its announcement post about reopening drew global attention: as of writing it had been liked 622,000 times, shared 405,000 times and seen by up to 10 million people worldwide. Ambassador Arto Haapea said the team was surprised and hadn’t analysed why, theorising the post merely rode the same algorithm as a previous viral “Finnish Dinner Date” clip that reached 8m views with 163,000 likes. He added he still isn’t sure of the cause, suggesting people sought good news amid global turmoil.
items.title: Finland’s Canberra Embassy Went Viral Over a Staff Training Post

items.summary: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI and a new framework called AlphaProof Code to mathematically verify key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol in four weeks. The work independently validates protections behind apps like Google Messages and WhatsApp, found no new vulnerabilities, correctly identified known ones on older versions, but did not cover the entire mobile app.
items.title: Google DeepMind formally verifies core Signal cryptography with AI

items.summary: Nvidia stock rose in premarket trading on Wednesday, recovering part of losses from a $480 billion market value crash tied to an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. Shares fell 4.3% Monday and another 5.47% Tuesday before closing at $168.89 after opening at $178.67.
items.title: Nvidia rebounds after $480 billion wipeout amid Jensen Huang investigation

items.summary: Nvidia has hired New York-based Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation into the relationship between its chief executive, Jensen Huang, and an alleged Chinese spy. The $4.1tn (£3tn) chipmaker engaged the firm after reports that Huang had been having an affair with Alice Huang, who was also an Nvidia customer. Following initial denials, Huang admitted on Sunday he had been unfaithful to his wife without referring directly to Ms Huang. On the same day, Nvidia announced a probe into reports that Huang “has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”. The scandal has wiped $430bn off Nvidia’s value as shareholders gauge its impact.
items.title: Nvidia hires law firm over Jensen Huang spy probe

items.summary: CoreWeave jumped 10 per cent on Wednesday, igniting a rally in battered AI cloud stocks as strong revenue growth and signals of reduced borrowing eased bubble fears. The move lifted backer Nvidia by 5 per cent after its slide over CEO Jensen Huang's conduct allegations. Analysts praised the quarter but warned CoreWeave could be among the first hit when capacity crunches ease.
items.title: CoreWeave Stock Surge Lifts Nvidia Amid AI Bubble Fears

items.summary: An AI-generated trailer titled Huang's Honeypot imagines Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang meeting Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang in a fictional spy romance, presenting it as a 2028 Netflix release. The clip turns real-world allegations into fiction and does not depict actual events. Its circulation comes amid reports that US intelligence officials suspected Alice Huang of links to China's Ministry of State Security over Nvidia chip sales, though the allegations have not been independently established publicly. Nvidia said it had no reason to believe trade secrets were compromised and its board announced an independent investigation.
items.title: AI Spy Trailer Recasts Jensen Huang Controversy as Fiction

items.summary: An ECB adviser told a panel at the Web Summit in Lisbon that Christine Lagarde's early departure as president of the European Central Bank will not hold up the digital euro. Alessandro Giovannini, adviser to the programme manager of the project, cited the pilot due next year and EU lawmakers' commitment to agree the law by the end of 2026. He dismissed privacy fears, describing offline payments that leave no trace for the ECB to see. Europe trails China's digital yuan since 2019 and the US GENIUS Act, but Giovannini said "we are not losing time." The pilot involves 36 banks starting in the second half of 2027, with first issuance aimed for 2029.
items.title: ECB official says Lagarde's exit will not delay digital euro

items.summary: Nvidia has reportedly received a 60 per cent target cut, with Baird downgrading the stock to 'Neutral' from 'Outperform'. The firm warned that AI hyperscaler capex could slow to 40 per cent growth or slightly less in 2027. Nvidia shares have plunged 17 per cent in the past week, taking their monthly decline to 25 per cent, amid controversy involving CEO Jensen Huang.
items.title: Baird Cuts Nvidia Target Amid AI Slowdown and CEO Scandal

items.summary: A Korea Herald report says Google expanding sales of its tensor processing units to external customers could create high-bandwidth memory opportunities for South Korean makers beyond Nvidia. Counterpoint Research forecasts HBM bit demand for custom AI server chips rising 35-fold between 2024 and 2028, though converting this into orders may be hard as capacity is heavily committed.
items.title: Google’s AI chip push may open HBM demand for Samsung and SK hynix

items.summary: Reuters reports Nvidia shed about US$430 billion in market value over two sessions as allegations emerged that Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang aided at least US$7.5 billion in chip shipments to China. The New York Times reported Rubio briefed Trump aboard Air Force One in May, while Axios cited a classified memo warning Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick about the affair; Reuters could not verify either report. Schumer demanded tighter export curbs and Nvidia hired outside counsel Joon Kim to investigate. Huang apologized internally but no details were given.
items.title: Nvidia CEO's China ties spark scrutiny and stock plunge

items.summary: Jensen Huang of Nvidia has endured a difficult week after admitting an extramarital affair while his company and the FBI investigate possible ties to Chinese intelligence. Social media users have flooded him with AI-generated memes, using the same technology he helped popularize. The article presents these jokes as examples circulating online.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang faces AI meme backlash amid scandal

items.summary: Finland granted provisional approval on Wednesday for Tesla's Assisted Driving system (TAD) after the automaker renamed it from "Full Self-Driving" and tightened speed-control settings, allowing its use on Finnish roads ahead of an EU-wide vote expected this winter. Traficom said Finland has 8,000-9,000 TAD-compatible Teslas, around 0.3 per cent of the fleet, so it felt able to move forward.
items.title: Finland Clears Tesla Assisted Driving Tech After Changes

items.summary: A Federal Reserve official warned of a “large correction” in stock prices if AI returns disappoint, as the frontier lab prepares its expected $1.4 trillion IPO. Fed Governor Michelle Bowman cited $800 billion in AI-related debt and off-balance-sheet liabilities, saying shocks may slow the buildout. Anthropic’s valuation is pegged at $90.4 billion for a Nov. 18 pricing.
items.title: Fed official warns Anthropic IPO could trigger market correction

items.summary: Semafor analyzed 42 podcast interviews with Jensen Huang since early 2022, finding his rhetoric on China grew more admiring and his stance on export controls more critical after the US restricted Nvidia’s made-for-China chip in 2025. Mentions of China rose roughly sixfold; he invoked the American tech stack 34 times across eight interviews since July 2025, saying 50% of world AI researchers are Chinese or in China. The analysis also notes an alleged affair with a suspected spy under board and congressional review.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Softens China View Amid Export Crackdown

items.summary: An emerging case has shaken the artificial intelligence industry amid rising U.S.-China tensions, spotlighting Nvidia’s near-monopoly in global technology. The company announced an investigation into Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang (Huang Le), a Chinese-origin businesswoman accused of spying for Beijing and passing AI policy information to Chinese authorities. Nvidia states it has “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.” The firm controls roughly 80% to 90% of the AI accelerator market by revenue, generating more than $100 billion annually. Its chips are central to U.S.-China tensions and export-control disputes dating back to 2022.
items.title: Nvidia’s chip dominance draws China espionage probe

items.summary: The article links an alleged Chinese espionage plot tied to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s admission of an extramarital affair with a woman suspected of being a Beijing spy to other industrial espionage cases. It notes the U.S. has investigated Huang for nearly a year, and cites Huawei as accused by the Justice Department of stealing trade secrets from Cisco Systems and T-Mobile since 2018; Huawei rejected the allegations. The piece also recounts AMSC’s near-bankruptcy after Sinovel stole wind turbine technology in 2018, McLaren’s $100 million penalty for possessing Ferrari information in Formula One's ‘Spygate’ scandal of 2007, and Procter & Gamble’s settlement with Unilever over contractors rummaging through trash. Many details remain alleged or denied.
items.title: Industrial espionage scandals that echo Nvidia's Jensen Huang case

items.summary: IBM ends visa and employment-based green card sponsorship for its US-based Consulting division, per an internal memo, amid a broader pullback in foreign hiring. Affected employees have until the end of 2026 to relocate abroad or leave; those staying must find another sponsoring employer. IBM cited changing client requirements and local skills availability. The company's H-1B approvals fell from nearly 3,000 in FY 2024 to 1,611 in fiscal year 2026.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa and Green Card Sponsorship for Consulting Division

items.summary: Singapore Airlines reported a 43.9% fall in first-half net profit to $134 million for its 2027 financial year, citing sustained high fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict. Revenue rose 16.8% to $11.3 billion on stronger passenger and cargo demand. The group said measures like fare adjustments do not fully offset rising fuel prices, though it remains positioned to manage volatility.
items.title: Singapore Airlines Reports Sharp First-Half Profit Drop Amid High Fuel Costs

items.summary: OpenAI announced a beta of Businesses in ChatGPT, adding two features—Business Hub and Business Agents—that let users ask companies directly about products and services. OpenAI said private chats would not be shared with businesses; only aggregated activity data at minimum thresholds would be provided.
items.title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Business Hub and Agents Feature

items.summary: The International Energy Agency reports that over 90% of major Chinese solar PV manufacturers are reporting net losses, with cumulative losses rising from around $4.4 billion in 2024 to almost $5.5 billion last year as higher module prices have failed to restore profitability. The agency notes signs of stabilisation and predicts continued industry consolidation through 2031.
items.title: IEA Warns China Solar Industry Faces Widespread Losses Amid Global Overcapacity

items.summary: ByteDance plans a Muse-like voice agent in coming weeks, co-founder Zhang Yiming said at an all-hands meeting. He sees ByteDance competing with Anthropic and OpenAI by 2029 or 2030, though the meeting was private.
items.title: ByteDance Plans Muse-Like AI Agent to Close Gap With US Labs

items.summary: Dario Amodei once wanted OpenAI to stop accepting money from Peter Thiel, whose $1.25 million backed Donald Trump’s 2016 campaign and which he called “morally worthy of condemnation.” A decade later, Founders Fund invested about $1.25 billion in the company Anthropic co-founded, where Amodei left amid tensions before its Nasdaq listing.
items.title: Anthropic CEO's Past Push for Thiel Money Back

items.summary: During Diwali in Vasai-Virar, a 21-year-old labour contractor named Vineetkumar seriously injured his hand while attempting to light an airborne sky-shot firecracker directly in his palm for a social media reel. The blast severely burned and extensively damaged the hand, requiring 72 stitches after complex surgery at Appasaheb Thorat Hospital in West Vasai. His condition is stable following plastic surgery performed by expert doctors.
items.title: Diwali Firecracker Blast Seriously Injures Mumbai Youth in Hand

items.summary: Microsoft says November 2026 cumulative updates resolve USB audio issues affecting Windows users who installed security updates since September, when devices failed to start or produce sound. Symptoms included no audio output and Code 10 errors on server and client systems. Microsoft released out-of-band fixes in September for multichannel modes; the remaining problems are addressed now. Some users restored audio by switching to 2-channel mode.
items.title: Microsoft Resolves USB Audio Problems From September Updates

items.summary: A podcast asks how politics can be improved and notes that three in four people in Africa say elections are the best way to choose leaders, while only 37% are satisfied with their democracy. In the US, 16% trust the federal government, and voters name politicians as its biggest problem. Guests Rohini Pande of Yale and Katherine Casey of Stanford discuss experiments on pay, information for party gatekeepers and women's quotas.
items.title: Who enters politics?

items.summary: Nvidia is the world's biggest supplier of high-end chips for AI and data centres, with some estimates putting its market share over 80%. Chief executive and co-founder Jensen Huang recently admitted an extramarital affair; his partner Alice Huang has been accused of being a Chinese intelligence agent. Nvidia has played a key role in US efforts to restrict advanced chip access to China since 2022, though trade records indicate over US$3 billion crossed from Singapore to China in a single year. After the disclosure, its share price fell and it is reportedly under criminal investigation.
items.title: Nvidia's AI Dominance Threatened by Jensen Huang Scandal

items.summary: Anthropic’s initial public offering drew orders for multiple times the stock on offer, according to Bloomberg. Through an IPO and private placement, Anthropic and its co-founders could raise up to $90.4 billion combined at the top of the price range, surpassing SpaceX’s debut as a record market launch. The company targets roughly $1.4 trillion in valuation, below earlier expectations.
items.title: Anthropic IPO Oversubscribed as Roadshow Begins

items.summary: According to Bloomberg, OpenAI generated about $10 billion in revenue for the three months ended September, its first quarter at that level. Its operating loss was $10.9 billion. Annualized revenue stood at roughly $50 billion. Revenue rose about 50% from the second quarter and nearly tripled year over year. OpenAI is finalizing a funding round valuing it at $1.25 trillion after pushing its public listing to next year.
items.title: OpenAI's Revenue and Losses Both Crossed $10 Billion in Q3

items.summary: Dave Goldblatt created Because of AI, an unfunded research site tracking documented cases where AI delivered measurable benefits and where it fell short. It launched October 23 and runs largely autonomously with AI tools updating its data. Public sentiment surveys cited suggest limited confidence in government regulation and growing fatigue about AI coverage.
items.title: Former Facebook engineer builds AI benefits database amid public skepticism

items.summary: OpenAI launched Business Hub in ChatGPT, a beta feature letting companies claim profiles, verify ownership, upload product feeds with prices and availability, and build agents. It targets the 1.2 billion weekly users. OpenAI says it will not share chats with businesses, keeps analytics aggregate for privacy, labels sponsored placements separately from regular responses, and plans expansion to more countries and categories.
items.title: OpenAI Adds Businesses Feature and AI Agents to ChatGPT

items.summary: Jensen Huang addressed his affair with Alice Huang in closed-door meetings, apologising without taking questions as Nvidia moved on to business. He had earlier admitted the relationship via company-wide email while omitting her name. The board launched an independent investigation through Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz; employees described the mood as sad.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Apologises After Affair Revelation

items.summary: The Beverage Container Return Scheme (BCRS) says it is studying arrangements to better manage commercial return volumes and keep public-facing machines accessible for individual consumers. Large supermarkets over 200 sq m are already mandated to set up return points, while mall operators may register interest as voluntary return points at bcrs.sg/return-points.
items.title: BCRS Studies Ways To Manage Commercial Return Volumes

items.summary: A CGTN commentator argues that the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee's emphasis on full, rigorous Party self-governance reinforces rather than undermines the Party's credibility. The commentary frames grassroots policy distortion as a structural governance defect rooted in power-responsibility mismatches and biased performance values, noting it is not unique to China but extends globally. It presents a vertically connected organizational system with two-way accountability as an institutional solution that preserves policy intent from top to bottom. Citing the 2020 World Bank review of Brazil's Bolsa Familia program, the author suggests these approaches may offer lessons for Global South countries.
items.title: Party self-governance strengthens Party credibility and image

items.summary: Army jawan Saurabh Tomar, 28, of the President's Bodyguard regiment stationed at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, said he is safe and undergoing treatment in Meerut after being shot in the head allegedly by two neighbours over an old rivalry on Diwali night while visiting his native village Gopalpur Khadana near Baghpat in Uttar Pradesh. He told reporters: 'I am safe.'
items.title: President's Bodyguard soldier shot in UP says he is safe

items.summary: Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal criticised the Congress, saying Sonia Gandhi gave a “clean chit” to those responsible for killing thousands of innocent Sikhs in 1984. In a post on X he urged Punjab Congress leaders to break their silence and asked whether they endorse Rajiv Gandhi’s decision not to deploy Army units in Delhi. Badal pointed to passages from Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, which she wrote about Indira Gandhi ordering Operation Blue Star.
items.title: Sukhbir Badal Demands Congress Leaders Break Silence Over Gandhi Remarks

items.summary: The Centre made electric vehicles the default choice for government staff-car procurement, though conventional cars remain purchasable with justification. The move lifted nine automobile stocks; M&M climbed 4.81% to Rs 3,449 and Ola Electric Mobility advanced 3.53% to Rs 35.16 on s0.
items.title: Centre's EV procurement policy lifts electric-vehicle stocks

items.summary: The CPC describes its 'self-revolution' as extending beyond internal Party discipline to improve governance, create a better business environment and support economic development. In Yiwu, reforms are helping businesses overcome trade bottlenecks and deliver goods overseas faster. The broader goal is a government responsive to the needs of businesses and the public.
items.title: CPC Frames Self-Revolution as Driver of Growth and Better Lives

items.summary: The Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission approved a petition by Nidar Utilities Panvel LLP (NUPLLP) to adopt a short-term power procurement tariff of ₹5.30 per kWh and validated its Power Purchase Agreement with Manikaran Power Limited (MPL). The commission found the process, conducted through an electronic tender on the DEEP portal, compliant despite only one bidder participating. The rate is lower than NUPLLP’s previous ₹5.35 per kWh.
items.title: MERC Approves ₹5.30 Short-Term Power Tariff for Panvel SEZ

items.summary: On November 4 China Telecom reported that a joint verification by China Telecom, Yangtze Optical Fibre and Cable (YOFC) and ZTE over a 1,007.48-kilometer link achieved simultaneous bidirectional signal transmission at 64 Tb per second in each direction. Test technicians said a signal took just 3.43 milliseconds one way across the 1,000-kilometer link.
items.title: China Telecom and partners complete hollow-core fiber transmission test

items.summary: During an inspection tour in Shanghai on Monday and Tuesday, Chinese Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing stressed the need to steadily advance deep integration of technological and industrial innovation. He called for aligning high-quality sci-tech supply with industrial demand, strengthening basic research, and empowering traditional industries through margin technologies (Xinhua).
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Stresses Industrial Innovation Push During Shanghai Visit

items.summary: During a handover ceremony in Chengdu on November 10, 2026, China transferred eight bone fragments recovered from a glacier more than 5,000 meters above sea level to the United States. The remains were found by Jianchuan Museum during expeditions near Nyingchi and are believed to belong to US airmen who went missing along the Hump Route in World War II after lying for more than 80 years. He Jiang of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Archives and DPAA forensic expert Colin Alexander Eliot signed the transfer document, witnessed by representatives from both countries. The airmen's identities have yet to be established; DNA testing will follow once they reach the United States.
items.title: China Returns WWII Hump Route Airmen Remains in Chengdu

items.summary: Transport and public services across Spain faced serious disruption during the first general strike in 14 years, called by main unions over affordable housing and high living costs. UGT leader Pepe Álvarez said turnout was "massive," while CC OO's Unai Sordo described it as "very significant." Power usage fell 7.5% on Wednesday, though that is below the more than 15% drop during the last strike in 2012. Rental prices remain steep: a 50 m² apartment averaged €1,170 monthly against an average gross salary of about €2,460 (£2,056), roughly half of which housing experts recommend for affordability. Business groups disputed the scale and motives as elections approach on 29 November.
items.title: Spain's First General Strike in 14 Years Disrupts Transport and Services

items.summary: Martin Rolfe, Nats boss, said he was “the most disliked person in the UK” after air traffic control systems failed twice in September 2026. On 8 September, about 8,000 flights were expected and 6,000 flew; on 21 September more than 200 were cancelled at Prestwick. Rolfe said he had not considered resigning despite calls from Ryanair’s Michael O’Leary, while the Civil Aviation Authority reviews findings for a report in early 2027.
items.title: Nats CEO Calls Himself Most Disliked After September Flight Chaos

items.summary: Diesel on UK forecourts stays close to October's record high of £2 despite falling oil prices, the AA said, calling it 'dismal'. Average diesel cost 197p. Christopher Waller warned energy prices could stay elevated due to Hormuz tanker insurance and US refining limits. The AA noted another petrol cut may follow as wholesale costs fall.
items.title: UK Diesel Prices Remain Near Record Despite Falling Oil Costs

items.summary: At U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, Russia and Ukraine agreed a large exchange of prisoners of war, officials said Wednesday. Jared Kushner called it the biggest humanitarian release yet, with numbers to be finalized tomorrow. Vladimir Medinsky and Rustem Umerov confirmed the planned swap after two days of talks amid low hopes for a breakthrough.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree Large Prisoner Exchange

items.summary: A study recorded 20,927 dung beetles from 29 species in Kerala’s Vypin-Kadamakkudy barrier island system, more diversity than expected for an urbanising landscape. The article notes their ecological roles and worldwide presence, then lists threats: habitat loss and fragmentation, declining dung quality, flooding and salinity intrusion in Kerala, and veterinary drugs such as ivermectin that can render dung toxic to beetles.
items.title: Study Finds High Dung Beetle Diversity on Kerala Barrier Island

items.summary: The article explains cold weather payments in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, triggered by seven days of below-zero temperatures averaging 0C or lower. Each payment is worth £25 per week for recipients of certain benefits such as pension credit, income support and universal credit. More than 1.4 million were made during winter 2025-26. Scotland offers a separate automatic winter heating payment of £62 between December and February.
items.title: Cold Weather Payments Eligibility and Amounts Explained

items.summary: Savannah Kunovsky of Ideo argues that adding artificial intelligence to physical products is often driven by investor and shareholder pressure rather than genuine need, making some designs worse. She says the test for any feature—AI or otherwise—is whether it helps someone do what they are trying to do. When AI replaces something that already worked well, such as a stove knob or car control, users face slower, less reliable interfaces. Kunovsky recommends starting with people and tasks before technical feasibility, keeping instant actions physical, and building in human-override pathways so mistakes remain small rather than eroding trust.
items.title: When AI Integration Actually Helps Products

items.summary: The House effectively ended the impeachment of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth by voting 211 to 204 to send the articles back for committee review, a move that circumvents any floor vote and ensures it will not be addressed before Congress ends. The effort was reintroduced by Rep. Thomas Massie on Monday. Separately, House Republicans voted to replace Speaker Mike Johnson with Jim Jordan as minority leader after midterm losses.
items.title: House Kills Hegseth Impeachment; GOP Names New Minority Leader

items.summary: Tundu Lissu, leader of the opposition Chadema party, was sentenced on November 6 to four years in prison for incitement following unrest during the October 2025 elections. He had been cleared of treason charges that could have meant a death sentence. Prosecutors accused him of encouraging a boycott over electoral concerns, citing social media posts. Lissu rejected the verdict as politically motivated; Chadema plans to appeal. Independent analyst Francis Ibrahim suggested it may signal political deescalation and early release for constitutional talks, though Chadema was excluded from July reconciliation meetings. Public opinion is divided on whether the trial was politically driven.
items.title: Lissu's Guilty Verdict and Tanzania's Political Tension

items.summary: In Angola’s central and southeastern highlands, local leaders have recruited experienced hunters as “Watchers” to curb illegal bushmeat hunting and monitor the Lisima Lya Mwono water tower. The elders approached environmental anthropologist Kerllen Costa four years ago after outsiders began poaching without permission; each village now nominates one Watcher who reports violations through smartphones. The landscape, larger than 150,000 square kilometers (58,000 square miles), is the source of major rivers feeding millions in neighboring countries and was designated a Ramsar wetland covering more than 50,000 km² (19,300 mi²). There are currently 75 Watchers, with plans to reach 100. Environmental scientist Luisa Escobar-Alvarado notes fire is not the main threat; instead she expects agricultural and timber expansion from external actors could worsen it. Costa stresses a strong push for community-managed livelihoods to sustain stewardship.
items.title: Angolan Hunters Guard a Ramsar Wetland Through Local Watch Programs

items.summary: The Devils Hole pupfish, one of Earth's rarest fish and classified as endangered, is growing inside a water-filled cavern deep underground in Death Valley, California. Conservationists boosted the population by introducing captive-raised fish and providing supplemental feed made of mysid shrimp, water fleas, and blood worms. In spring surveys, scuba divers counted 77 fish; in the latest survey they counted 137, nearly double the earlier total.
items.title: Devils Hole pupfish population rebounds in Death Valley survey

items.summary: A BloombergNEF report says developers of AI datacentres across the US, UK and mainland Europe have proposals to build on-site gas-fired plants creating 181GW of capacity because grid connections are delayed. The research warns this could emit about 345m metric tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent a year in the US – if planned – while by 2035 demand may nearly quadruple to 2,354 terawatt-hours. Critics say these stations will lock in high emissions for years.
items.title: AI Datacentre Developers Plan Large-Scale On-Site Gas Power Stations

items.summary: A researcher argues that migration from east Africa and the Horn of Africa is commonly misread as a mass movement toward Europe when most people actually move within the region or to Gulf states and southern Africa. Citing UN Refugee Agency 2026 data, Uganda hosts about 2.05 million refugees and asylum-seekers, followed by Ethiopia with 1.02 million, Sudan with 910,000 and Kenya with 879,000. The author says dominant narratives overemphasise smuggling and border control while overlooking intra-African mobility, poverty’s complicated role and migrants’ own perspectives, calling for better data on continental movement and more legal labour avenues.
items.title: East African Migration Is Mostly Regional, Not Europe-Bound

items.summary: A political communication specialist previews Cabo Verde’s presidential election on 15 November 2026, framing it as a test of the country’s stable democratic institutions. The nation has held peaceful power transfers for over three decades since independence in 1975. A recent change of government brought the African Party for the Independence of Cabo Verde back to office after ten years under the Movement for Democracy. The two main contenders are José Maria Neves and Joana Rosa, with four smaller candidates unlikely to challenge them. The specialist argues that whether institutions function effectively will depend on how presidential powers are exercised when president and prime minister belong to opposing camps.
items.title: Cabo Verde’s Presidential Election and Institutional Balance
